# MGNO 架构评审综合建议（2026-09-24 夜，step-2 v1 训练进行中） ## 1. 一句话结论 主干不需要换。现有设计由四部分组成：对 q 线性的延拓、精确刚体分离、精确端口值、变分读出 Ŝ = ÊᵀKÊ。有了这四部分，晶格解就是学习试探空间里的 Ritz–Galerkin 解，同时还免费附带一个严格、不需要标签的误差下界。现在的瓶颈不在容量，而在三件事： - step-2 泛化为什么失败，还没有用合适的证据测过； - 训练用的 q 分布、以及最坏方向 μ 所在的尾部，与晶格实际用到的方向不匹配； - 下游没有任何可信度信号。 建议的顺序是：先拿 v1 的检查点做一轮零成本诊断，再按判据做只动几何路径的低风险加固，同时加入晶格情境下的采样。虚拟边缘续延头、45 节点 GP 面模板、粗层改造，都等诊断结果满足条件再做。 --- ## 2. 瓶颈在哪里（按证据） ### 2.1 step-2 泛化：问题最关键，证据却最弱 - **现有证据不够用。** 目前的失败证据几乎全来自单几何网络的零样本测试（力类 107–2236%，r1 达 1e3 倍）。只见过一个几何的网络过拟合是意料之中的，这些数字分不清是架构不稳定，还是网络根本没学过这类几何。 - **有两种机制，代码里都找得到依据。** - **软方向放大。** 力类方向的 Rayleigh 商中位数是 1.8e-7，宏观类约 1e-4。同样的相对振幅误差，在软方向上的能量代价要高 1e2–1e3 倍，几个百分点的振幅误差就能产生 100–400% 的能量误差。任何架构都会有这个问题，只能靠数据覆盖和尾部训练压下去。 - **增益失控或垃圾值。** FULL0020→dev_0002 的宏观类误差 1745%、随机场 869%，约为零参数调和延拓的 40 倍，合理的插值不会差到这种程度。代码里对应的因素有： - 槽位系数是 0.2·MLP，没有界； - 延拓权重是 softplus，没有上界； - 大约 40 个受几何调制的线性级串联； - 输入特征 ld = log(d3/本几何中位数)；weak 定义为本几何中位数的 1%，而且这个 weak 同时决定 fringe 层的作用范围（models.py:119、336–337；prep_data.py:123）。 结果是特征的含义随厚度分布漂移。 - **首次进池最坏比 106→4.7 不能当作架构尾部的证据。** 它由 k=8、4 次随机起点的幂迭代算出，没有收敛，只是下界；而且正好落在前 3k 步学习率热身期，网络又是从单几何 r2 出发的。它能说明跨几何的结构学得动，仅此而已。 - **训练器本身会混淆测量。** - 池里 3 个几何、每 300 步换入一个，60k 步只走 1.35 遍，每个几何每次驻留约 300 步，学习率最高 1e-3。 - 探针是 order[:12]（train2.py:243），在 10k–40k 之间测到的主要是遗忘，而不是泛化。 - validate() 只报能量的类均值，没有灵敏度、p90、μ，也没有分族数字。 - best.pt 按"最大类均值能量"选，不一定是过门最好的模型。 ### 2.2 step-1 残余精度：尾部加分布偏移 - **能量误差是场误差的平方。** 库误差 1.8–2.4% 对应能量范数下约 13–15% 的场误差；μ = 1.31–1.48 意味着最坏方向的场误差达 56–69%。门之所以能过，靠的是 Galerkin 配对：延拓误差 5–10% 和界面误差 3–9% 符号相反，在结构上互相抵消到 2–3%。 **推论：** 网络自己的场必须和它自己的变分反力成对使用。任何局部后修正、换一个反力、或所谓"精确恢复"，都会退回到单侧误差。 - **界面误差由 μ 控制，而 μ 目前只报告、不训练。** - 记 Δ = Ŝ−S ⪰ 0，ΔR = 0。单个学习胞造成的晶格端口误差满足 ‖δU‖/‖q‖_S ≤ √((1−1/μ_eff)·ε_q)，其中 μ₋F ≤ μ_eff ≤ μ（μ₋F 指共享面固定时的值）。 - 代入 μ = 1.31–1.48、ε_q = 2–2.4%，界为 7–9%，实测 3.3–9.3%。nbr_z 载荷的 ε_q ≈ 1%，界约 5.7%，实测 4.8%。 - 训练损失是 mean log ê。它对误差 2% 的方向和误差 100 倍的方向给出的梯度是同一量级，并不偏向尾部。 - step-2 的对抗搜索只有 8 个向量、4 次迭代，每次进池就覆盖，远弱于 step-1 的做法（每 500 步热启动、缓冲 256 个向量）。 - **q 分布有偏移。** 把精确的晶格端口数据喂给网络，单看延拓部分的灵敏度误差是 5.3–9.9%；而在样本库上只有 0.6–1.5%。代码确认了原因： - force/face/support 三类都是把端口节点上采样的光滑场直接当节点力，虚拟边缘节点也受力（prep_data.to_ports 只做了 reshape）； - 弹簧刚度取 α × 面平均对角（prep_geo.py:62–65），把虚拟边缘夹得比它自身刚度硬 1–100 倍； - 而验收门用的是按面力一致的载荷加上与母胞粘接； - 设计文档 6.3 要求的"三分之一一致载荷"没有实现，"被拖着走"的状态也从未采样。 另外，灵敏度里有一部分一阶误差不受 Galerkin 保护（dK/dτ 中不与 K 成比例的部分）。所以，拿到晶格情境下的灵敏度标签，比加大样本库上灵敏度损失的权重更关键。 - **虚拟边缘。** - 在 r1 v0 上，36% 的误差能量落在 GP 项，45% 的体误差落在含 weak 节点的单元。 - GP 面超边只取了 0–4 层节点中的 1–3 层（models.py `_face_setup`），而 Q2 的两个跳跃泛函需要第 0 层和第 4 层。 - 不过这些份额是在 v0 上测的，没有按单元数归一。切割胞里含 weak 节点的单元可能本来就占一半左右。 - 单元层和面层交替堆叠，可以组合出 5 层泛函，所以限制在于每层的表达力，而不是"看不见"。 - MGNO2 上的份额还没有测。 - **两点需要注意：** - nbr_z 的"界面 4.8% / 延拓 1.0%"是在 d2 之前的 MGNO2 上测的（那时总误差 4.4%），d2（3.10%）还没有做拆分； - 单个载荷有 ±0.2–0.3 个百分点的波动完全可能。 fp32 不是瓶颈：两条 fp32 路径的能量差是 5–7e-6，约为 ε 的 0.03%。 ### 2.3 下游使用 - **坏胞会静默失败。** 不管权重是什么，Ŝ ⪰ S 都成立，所以坏胞只会让晶格偏刚。PCG 照常收敛，灵敏度却被污染，目前也没有任何报警。 - 读出过程其实已经算出了 r = Kû。因为端口精确，而精确延拓是 K-调和的，所以 r_I = K_II·e_I，并且 Δ(q) = qᵀ(Ŝ−S)q = r_Iᵀ K_II⁻¹ r_I。 - 对任意内部向量 w，有 (wᵀr_I)² / (wᵀK_II w) ≤ Δ(q)。这是一个严格的下界，不需要求解，目前还没有用上。 - **当前的门低估了部署时的误差。** - 现在只有被测胞是学习的，它的误差会按能量占比打折：测试载荷打 0.13–0.41 折，邻居载荷打 0.0013–0.011 折。 - C−Ĉ 在各个学习胞上符号相同、直接相加，所以全部用学习胞的晶格会更苛刻。部署透镜估计 2 胞全学习时柔度误差约 2–3.5%，这个数还没测。 - **step 3 才需要处理的问题。** - weak 用硬阈值，导致 Ĉ(τ) 在固定拓扑内跳变，没有一致的梯度。 - 每个 FULL 胞约需 1.2 GB 网络记录加 2.4 GB 的 K（估计）。 - 晶格求解目前只有 2 胞的稠密 Cholesky。 --- ## 3. 推荐改动 **约束核对。** - 下面所有主线项都是完全学习的：精确 K 只出现在读出、损失和监控里。 - 证书里的 Krylov 迭代只用于监控，从不进入场。 - SGNO 类方法和测试时自适应只能作为单独标注的退路。 **实现优先级。** 前景相当时，优先选只改几何路径的项（B1–B3），因为它们复用已经验证过的 q 路径核。改 q 路径核（B5）要同时改三处：models 稠密路径、sparse_layers 的手写反向、fastnet 的显式伴随，然后重跑 t_fast 验证。 ### A. 先做的廉价诊断（不改架构） **GPU 使用规则。** v1 峰值显存 28.4/31.4 GB，训练期间只做 CPU 和日志类的诊断。需要分解的诊断要等 v1 结束，原因有二： - 可能把 v1 挤到显存溢出； - 守护脚本续跑会改变 RNG 流，v1 就不再是干净的对照。 | # | 回答的问题 | 做法 | 判据 → 下一步 | 时机 | |---|---|---|---|---| | A0 | 保住证据、修好工具 | ① 外部脚本在每次 EVAL 后把 last.pt 另存为带步号的文件（train2 每次都会覆盖）
② zs_eval 改用 `cfg.get('cases')`
③ evalnet/diag_lat 的邻居改成参数，指向本族 FULL 母胞
④ diag_error 扩展到 support/face 两类

在 r2 上把现有检查点等权平均：凸性保证它不差于成员均值，同时能看出成员之间的误差相关性。 - 在 3 个 val 几何上做 300 步无标签自适应：用来区分是"容量不够"还是"泛化不够"。这只是诊断，不进主线。 ### B. 核心架构改动 各项都是完全学习的。 **B1 有界几何系数（G1a；把 P5 的延拓幅度上限、P2 的 tanh 部分、L7 的上限合并进来）——建议作为 v2 的默认项** - **模块：** slot_head / fslot_head / slot_head_x / restrict_head，以及 MGCache 的输入。 - **改法：** - 槽位系数改成 a = A·tanh(a_raw/A)。A 取训练几何上 |系数| 的 p99.9 的 2–3 倍，在 v1 最终检查点上标定，存为固定缓冲。 - 延拓权重改成 w = w_max·tanh(softplus(r)/w_max) + 1e-3。 - 矩比 M/vol 截断到 [−1,1]：在中心化的局部坐标下，合法值本来就在这个范围内。ld 也做截断。 - 每个几何记录系数的饱和比例，作为免费的分布外（OOD）分数。 - **针对的问题：** O(1) 量级的增益失控，例如宏观类 1745%。 - **预期（估计）：** 去掉极端尾部，均值基本不降。p99.9 处的值最多变约 8%，中位数几乎不变。每层的界是 1 + 27HA_aA_b‖W‖，这个界太松，挡不住 24 层的复合放大。它真正的作用是保证分布外特征最多饱和到训练范围，而不是无限放大。 - **风险和成本：** 低。步时增加不到 1%。热启动近似保持原函数，需要 LR 3e-4 的短微调。只在几何路径加 LayerNorm 的版本（G1b）留给从头训练的 run。 - **验证：** 从 v1 最终检查点接着训 1 万步，与共享对照比较。通过条件： - val 各几何力类均值的最大值 ≤ 对照的 0.6 倍； - 首次进池 Ritz 值的中位数 ≤ 对照的 0.7 倍； - 各类均值变化在 ±5% 以内。 **B2 几何一致的输入特征（G3，加上 D4 的特征部分）——由 A1/A3 触发** - **模块：** MGCache.nfeat，MGNO2 的 fringe 掩码。 - **改法：** - 把 ld 换成 log(d3/d_ref(t))。d_ref 是某类 Q2 节点（顶点、棱、面、体心）在全实心时的解析值。所有几何共用 E、ν、h，所以 d_ref 是常数。 - 新增软 weak 分数 s = σ((log₁₀(d3/d_ref)+2)/0.15)。 - 新增到端口的图跳数，以及到裁切面和盒面的有符号距离（截断在 6 个单元）。 - 分两步做：臂 1 只加新列，输入权重零初始化，旧掩码不动；臂 2 再把 fringe 层改到固定的超集掩码上，并按 s 平滑渐入。 - **保留 sin/cos 坐标。** 所有胞都是同一个 Schwarz-P 单胞，绝对相位是真实的几何信息，在 O_h 下协变。 - **针对的问题：** 同厚度 FULL 之间迁移误差 8.5%，不同厚度之间 2236%；weak 阈值随中位数移动，导致 fringe 层的作用范围跳变。 - **预期（估计）：** val 误差或训练-留出差距下降 10–25%。附带让 Ĉ(τ) 在固定拓扑内连续，这是 step 3 需要的。 - **风险和成本：** 低到中。特征计算只要毫秒级；改掩码后需要 2–5k 步重新学习。 **B3 按刚度份额散射（P2 与 G7a 的最小版）——由 A4 触发** - **模块：** 只改 β 值和散射归一化，q 路径核不动。 - **改法：** 散射改成 dX_i = Σ_e π_{e,i} Y_{e,i}，权重 π_{e,i} = ‖K_e[s,s]‖ / Σ_{e′∋i}‖K_{e′}[s,s]‖；GP 面用 γ‖G_f[s,s]‖。与旧的 1/deg 用可学的 λ 混合，λ 初始化为 0。 - **依据：** 精确解的边缘值满足 (Ku)_W = 0，本身就是强邻居节点的刚度加权组合。现在网络得靠 MLP 从 ld/5 这一个特征里合成 2–4 个数量级的刚度差。 - **去掉的部分：** 零和投影和 l1-Jacobi 守卫。"每层非扩张"并不成立（κ 不对称，W 无界），这两项降低表达力，又没有证据支持。 **B4 带门控的虚拟边缘续延头（L3；合并 P3、G7b）——由 A8 判定做不做** - **模块：** 输出级，放在 W_out 之后、端口覆盖之前。每个几何在 MGCache 里多一个几何算子 C。 - **改法：** u ← u + diag(g)·M_W(Cu − u)。 - C 只用网格、软 weak 分数和 vf 构造，不含 K。两种取法：AgFEM 根单元多项式在该点的值，或邻域非 weak 节点上的最小二乘仿射。两者都能精确再现刚体运动和均匀应变。 - 门控 g_w = σ(head) 初始化接近 0；四周全是空单元的节点初始化约 0.9。 - **保持不变的性质：** 对 q 线性、端口精确、刚体精确；Ŝ 仍然对称半正定且 ⪰ S。 - **针对的问题：** GP 加 weak 区的误差份额；均布节点力压力测试 5.3–8.5%；零样本时边缘区的多余能量。 - **预期（提案估计，以 A8 通过为前提）：** - 边缘误差份额约减半； - 力类和支撑类库误差从约 2.0% 降到 1.3–1.6%； - 在新几何上，边缘能量被"强节点误差 × 延拓常数（2–8）"控制住。 - 不指望它单独修好 nbr_z，最终与 C1 一起捆绑进入。 - **不做的部分：** CVaR 和八分区标签。 **C3 尾部：先加强对抗搜索并把 μ 纳入验证，Ritz 尾损失视 A6 结果再定（合并 obj-P3/P5 和 EA-P4）** - **先做（不改损失）：** - 每个几何在主机上保留一个 16–32 向量的对抗缓冲，跨访问不丢弃； - 首次访问时用 Neumann 分解做幂迭代，以 force/face 向量作种子，k=16； - 分解只在几何首次访问时做； - 每批按固定的类配比抽样，不再用多项式随机抽； - 权重 EMA，衰减 0.9997； - validate() 增加灵敏度的均值和 p90、分族数字、5 个固定几何上的 μ； - 探针改成固定的分层抽样，并记录每个几何距上次访问的步数； - 选模型改为综合看灵敏度、p90 和 μ。 - **按条件开启的项：** - 按难度采样（上限 3/N，最后 10% 的步数回到均匀）只在 max/median >3 时开； - **D1 残差证书（D1 与 G5 合并）——现在就做，零风险。** - **零参数版：** - 取 w = D_II⁻¹ r_I，D_II 是 NETDATA 里已有的 3×3 对角块； - 或者在 m=8–16 维的块 Jacobi-Krylov 子空间上算 bᵀG⁻¹b。 - **能得到什么：** - 对每个查询，μ(q) ≥ 1/(1 − ε_lb)； - 在晶格层面，Σ_c Δ_lb,c(q̂_c) ≤ C − Ĉ，也就是柔度误差的一个严格下界； - 所有臂共用一个对照：d2 再训 1 万步，配比、种子相同，最高学习率 3e-4。不要用 e 臂作对照，因为它没有 face 类。 - 顺序：C2 → C1 臂 A → C1 臂 B → 按条件决定的 B4 / B5 / C3 尾损失。 - 判据： - 看 12 个门载荷的误差分布加压力测试，不要只盯 nbr_z 这一项； - 各类库误差变差不超过 5–10%； - 同时报告 μ 和 diag_lat 的拆分结果； - 胜出的臂用 2 个种子确认。 **阶段 4（每臂约 1.5 h）：step-2 续训臂。** - 从 v1 最终检查点出发，LR ≤3e-4，训 1–2 万步，共用一个续训对照。 - 候选臂：B1、B2 臂 1、B6（需你同意）、B3（触发时才做）。 - 判据： - 按族配对比较，4 个 val 族里至少 3 个同向改善； - 看各几何的 max 和 p90； - 看 5 个固定几何上的 μ，以及证书的报警数。 - 注意：续训臂会低估从头训练的收益。 **阶段 5：** - 重新准备数据：加入 C1 的新类、存 F、修复 NaN 几何，约 3–4 GPU 小时； - 跑 v2 全程，约 5 h，包含训练器 v2 和所有胜出项； - 在留出族上跑全学习晶格门，每个族用自己的 FULL 母胞； - 测试族（development）只在最终配置定下后用一次。 **统计把握度：** val 只有 4 个族，族间差异远大于 0.3–0.6% 的梯度噪声。要在大约 10 个臂之间做选择，必须坚持"至少 3/4 族同向改善，胜出者用 2 个种子"，否则很容易在 val 族上过拟合选择。 --- ## 5. 需要你拍板的事 1. **v1 是否跑完。** 建议跑完，作为唯一的干净对照。只有在 20k 时证实遗忘非常严重的情况下，才考虑提前停下，把 GPU 让给诊断。 2. **O_h 增广是否从"第二轮"提前进入 v2。** 你定的朝向范围要靠它；它会改变训练分布。 3. **全学习晶格门是否作为附加报告指标**，以及是否据此调整 step-2 的精度目标。门本身的定义不动，除非你另作决定。 4. **是否批准一次全量重新准备数据。** 约 3–4 GPU 小时，磁盘增加 30–50%，内容包括：一致面力、按刚度比例的弹簧、粘接类、F、以及 5 个 NaN 几何的 fp64 重算。粘接构型与门不相交，这条约定也需要你确认。 5. **μ 和 μ₋F 是否从"只报告"升格为训练目标和选模型的依据之一**（门本身不变）。选模型的标准相应从"最大类均值能量"改为综合看灵敏度、p90 和 μ。 6. **证书报警后怎么处理：** 整个胞走退路 A，还是走标注的测试时自适应。两者都在主线之外。 7. **B1/B2 的影响。** 它们会让热启动后的数字发生变化。按"结果不能悄悄改变"的要求，它们全部以对照臂的形式引入；是否接受它们作为 v2 的默认项，由你决定。 8. **O2（XP/XB 端口约定）** 仍然留到 step 3 接整体求解时再比较。

proposals.title: Ghost-penalty-consistent face hyperedges: full 45-node two-element stencil with jump-space gather/scatter
proposals.component: q path fine layers (MGNO2 ghost-face and fringe-face layers: _face_setup, fslot_head, Wf; sparse_layers.pattern/_mats/backward and fastnet._Hyper generalized from the hard-coded 27 slots to S slots)
proposals.mechanism:
Replace c.fn (27 slots = layers 1-3) with the true 45-node ghost stencil P_f (5 normal layers x 3x3, the offsets in GP_TEMPLATES_n32.npz). Let J (18x45) be the scalar ghost jump functionals: first- and second-normal-derivative jumps at the 9 face points (the scalar block of F_axis, 54x135 = J kron I3; verify the Kronecker form, else use the component block).

Per head h:
- Gather: alpha_f,.,h = J^T c_f,.,h, where the face head outputs 18 coefficients c per face.
- Scatter: beta_f,.,h = J^T d_f,.,h / fdeg.

The layer is then dX = sum_f P_f^T J^T D_f,h W_h J P_f X. This has the same algebraic form as the true ghost-penalty operator gamma sum_f P_f^T F^T F P_f, but with learned per-face rank-H couplings and channel mixing.

Properties:
- It annihilates every field that is one triquadratic across the two elements: rigid motions, affine fields and smooth bending curvature.
- It acts only on kinks, which is exactly what the ghost penalty prices.
- J is geometry-independent, so the layer transfers across geometries.

Warm start, function-preserving: embed the old 27-slot weights in the 45 slots, with zeros on layers 0 and 4. Then blend alpha = (1-lambda) alpha_old + lambda J^T c, with lambda learnable per layer, initialized at 0. Conservative sub-arm: 45 slots without the projection.
proposals.addresses: 36% of the force-direction error energy in the ghost-penalty term (r1 v0 block diagnosis). The fringe share of the error. Stress-test sensitivity 5.3-8.5%. Zero-shot spurious energy in the weak regions. Soft-mode (bending) pollution by the current 3-layer (1,-2,1) functional.
proposals.expected_gain: Ghost-penalty share of the error energy (diag_error ghost_share) roughly halved. Step-1 bank force/support/face errors down 15-30%. r2 y test-cell sensitivity 3.10% -> <=2.7%. Stress-test sensitivity 5.3-6.7% -> ~4%. Probably a larger relative gain on held-out geometries, because the stencil and J are geometry-independent.
proposals.risk: MGNO2's current ghost-penalty share may already be below v0's 36%, which would shrink the gain. Jump-only face layers can no longer carry smooth information across faces, but the element layers still do. Pattern memory for the face layers grows 1.67x. The J scaling between derivative orders must be left to the learned c.
proposals.cost: Face-layer gather/scatter cost x1.67, so +20-35% step time, since ghost faces are at least as many as cut elements. The face head outputs 18 instead of 27 numbers per head, so parameters go slightly down. Code: ~80 lines (S-slot generalization of sparse_layers.pattern lines 33-34 and 91-92, fastnet lines 36-37, face setup).
proposals.test:
(0) Unit checks: linearity, the adjoint identity (t_fast.py), and J P_f annihilating a random global triquadratic to 1e-6. Report diag_error ghost_share for the current d2 model as the baseline.
(1) Step-1 r2 A/B from mgno2_r2_d2/best.pt with the mg2_r2d2 recipe (lr 3e-4, 10k steps). Arms: control (d2 + 10k steps), 45-slot, 45-slot + jump projection. Report:
- bank val per class (energy and sensitivity)
- adversarial mu (k=16)
- diag_error ghost_share and weak_elems_share
- evalnet x/y gate plus the uniform-load stress test

Pass: ghost_share <= 0.5x control; force and face bank means >= 15% below control; gate x/y pass (r2 y <= 3.0%); stress-test sensitivity below control.
(2) zs_eval.py of all three arms on 0031-medium, 0031-heavy and dev_0000-heavy: mean force error below control.
(3) If (1) passes, run one step-2 arm with the s2_full config and seed. Use the running main line's 10k/20k checkpoints as the control, compared on the 20 held-out val geometries.

proposals.title: Jacobi-form element hyperedges: fixed diagonal-stiffness scales, zero-sum gathers, bounded O(1) slot weights (l1-Jacobi guard)
proposals.component: q path fine layers (element and fringe-element layers: MGNO._fine / MGNO2._hyper normalization, slot_head output parameterization) + geometry-path precompute
proposals.mechanism:
Precompute once per geometry:
- w_e,s = ||diag block s of K_e||_F from K_e = sum_m M_em T_m (E x 27)
- D_i = ||diag3_i||, already in NETDATA
- for ghost faces: w_f,s = gamma diag(F^T F)_s

Gather: a_e,s,h = sqrt(w_e,s) a~_e,s,h / sigma_e, where a~ = c_a tanh(raw/c_a) is projected so that sum_s sqrt(w_e,s) a~ = 0. This exactly annihilates locally constant states in every channel, i.e. local translations.

Scatter: b_e,s,h = sigma_e sqrt(w_e,s) b~_e,s,h / Dbar_i, where b~ = c_b tanh(raw/c_b) and sigma_e = sqrt(mean_s w_e,s) cancels. Dbar_i = max(D_i, l1 row bound of the layer), the hypre l1-Jacobi guard, which makes each layer non-expansive whatever the geometry features.

For a rank-H kappa_e = sum_h b~_h W_h a~_h^T, this is damped l1-Jacobi on an element-assembled operator sqrt(w) kappa sqrt(w):
- a weak node becomes a stiffness-share-weighted average of its strong neighbours in one layer;
- a weak sender barely moves strong nodes;
- the MLP only has to produce O(1) numbers.

Warm start: a learnable per-layer lambda in [0,1], initialized at 0, interpolates the old deg and unscaled forms with the new ones. Set c_a and c_b to 3x the 99.9th percentile on the training geometries, so clipping is inactive in-distribution.
proposals.addresses: Zero-shot gain blow-ups (macro 85-1745%, force up to 2236% mean). Step-2 first-entry worst ratios of 106/280/46. 45% of the body error in weak-node elements. The 2-4 decade stiffness contrast that the heads currently have to synthesize from a log(diag)/5 feature.
proposals.expected_gain: Held-out-geometry bank errors 25-50% lower at equal steps. Worst direction at first entry <= 10 instead of up to 280. Smaller train-geometry vs held-out gap. Step-1 accuracy unchanged or slightly better (weak-element share down).
proposals.risk: The sqrt(w) gather silences messages sent from weak nodes; if the network uses the fringe as a latent conduit, accuracy may drop (lambda lets training back off). The l1 guard can over-damp: monitor the effective step. Changing the parameterization mid-run needs the gentle warm start (lr <= 3e-4, per the warm-start lesson).
proposals.cost: Negligible: E x 27 plus N scalars per geometry, and one projection per head in the geometry path; no per-q cost. New parameters: one lambda per layer. ~60 lines.
proposals.test:
(0) Free pre-check on the d2 checkpoint, geometry path only, on r2 and on the zero-shot geometries (0031-medium, dev_0000, dev_0002):
- Has the net learned the Jacobi share? Check the correlation of log|beta_e,s|/deg with log(w_e,s/D_i).
- Compare the 99.9% quantiles of |alpha|, |beta| and the prolongation weight rw between training and unseen geometries.
- Run zs_eval.py with soft clipping only (no retraining). If the macro/GRF blow-ups shrink, coefficient-magnitude extrapolation is causal.

(1) Step-2 arm: s2_full config with the same seed, split, pool order and d2 warm start, 15k steps. Control: the running main line at 10k/15k.

Compare:
- EVAL val_mean per class (20 held-out)
- the train_geo probe gap (12)
- ADV ritz_top on each entry
- diag_error weak_elems_share and ghost_share on 3 val geometries

Pass: val force/support/face >= 25% below control; max first-entry ritz_top <= 10; probe errors within 10% of control.

proposals.title: Learned fringe condensation head: a local Schur-like block mapping strong anchors to weak nodes, with affine (quadratic where possible) reproduction
proposals.component: readout / wrapper (after W_out and the exact port overwrite in Geo.field and fastnet.field/field_T) + a new geometry-path pair head
proposals.mechanism:
The exact interior weak values satisfy (K u)_W = 0, so u_W = -K_WW^-1 K_W,rest u_rest. The ROUTES lesson is that weak nodes must stay paired with their strong anchors.

For each interior weak node w:
1. Anchors A(w) = non-weak nodes and port nodes of the elements and ghost faces containing w. Grow to the 2x2x2-element box if there are fewer than 10 (~30-60 anchors).
2. Phi_w,a = MLP(g_n(w), g_n(a), x_a - x_w, pooled patch embedding).
3. Project each row onto {sum_a Phi = 1, sum_a Phi (x_a - x_w) = 0}, plus the 6 quadratic moments when there are 20 or more anchors. The minimal-norm correction is a 4x4 or 10x10 solve on geometry-only data, done once per geometry. This is not a K solve.
4. u_w <- (1 - theta_w) u_w^net + theta_w sum_a Phi_w,a u_a, applied identically to x, y and z (the ghost penalty is componentwise). theta_w = sigmoid(head(g_n(w))), initialized near 0, which also softens the hard 1% weak threshold.

The result is linear in q, a sparse n_W x N matrix with a transpose adjoint. Rigid motions and affine fields continue exactly into the fringe.

Effects:
- Fringe values can no longer carry spurious amplitude, because the rows are bounded.
- The fringe continues the strong-side polynomial, so the surface energy density that dK/dtau samples comes out right.
proposals.addresses: The ~65% fringe share of the error energy (36% ghost penalty + 45% of the body error in weak elements, r1 v0). Extension-only sensitivity errors of 5-10% (sensitivity is supported on the cut elements). Uniform-load stress test 5.3-8.5%. Zero-shot 'large spurious energy in weak regions'.
proposals.expected_gain: Conditional on the oracle test. If the oracle local map leaves <= 0.2% excess energy: bank energy errors down 30-50%, extension-only sensitivity errors down to 2-4%, stress-test sensitivity roughly halved, and fringe-located zero-shot blow-ups removed structurally.
proposals.risk: The fringe sheets are connected (e.g. 2 components of ~10k nodes in FULL). If K_WW^-1 is not local, a local map cannot represent it. The oracle test decides, and a failure redirects effort to the two-continuum coarse space in P5. Anchors next to ports and very thin walls (1.4h at vf 0.1) may be scarce.
proposals.cost: Geometry path: +~0.8M pair MLP evaluations for FULL (20k weak x 40 anchors), about +10-20% of geometry-path time. Per q: one sparse matmul and its transpose, negligible. ~150 lines including the fastnet adjoint.
proposals.test:
(0) Oracle feasibility, no training. Use r1, r2, FULL and 3 step-2 geometries (thin tau, heavy cut, rotated variant). Compute exact fields with C.extend on the train and val banks. Replace the interior weak values by:
- (a) an affine least-squares continuation from the anchors;
- (b) the per-node least-squares Phi fitted on the 512x5 train-bank fields, i.e. the best local linear map;
- (c) a local exact patch condensation (ceiling).

Report, per class, the excess energy (u'-u)^T K (u'-u)/u^T K u (= dW^T K_WW dW, by interior harmonicity) and the 8-corner sensitivity error. Go if (b) gives <= 0.2% energy and <= 0.3% sensitivity on force, face and support.
(1) Step-1 r2 A/B from d2 (10k steps, lr 3e-4) versus the P1 control. Report bank val per class, diag_error weak and ghost shares, the evalnet gate and the stress test.

Pass: weak + ghost share halves; x/y gate pass; stress-test sensitivity <= 4%.
(2) zs_eval on the three zero-shot pairs.

proposals.title: Train and validate mu where the lattice transmits it: clamped-face Rayleigh-Ritz adversary, the interface bound as a metric, fp64 rigid wrapper
proposals.component: sampling/loss (adversarial on entry in train2.adversarial_on_load and trainlib.Geo.adversarial) + validation + inference wrapper precision (fastnet.field/field_T)
proposals.mechanism:
From the bound ||dq_free||_S/||q||_S <= sqrt((mu_-F - 1)(e_q - 1)), the direction set that matters for a dragged or partly glued cell is: box face F prescribed, all other ports free. That is the pencil (S_hat_-F, S_-F) on the non-F port DOFs.

On entry:
1. Pick 1-2 random faces F.
2. Build an fp32 factor of K with F's ports clamped and the other ports free (the prep_support factor with infinite springs).
3. Run block power iteration with Rayleigh-Ritz (same code as adversarial, with the clamped factor in place of neumann).
4. Add the top 8 directions to the adv bank.

Cheaper variant using the all-free Neumann factor already built: V = S^+ B_F R, with R = smooth self-equilibrated face tractions as in prep_face, then Ritz on (V^T S_hat V, V^T S V).

Add mu_-F (k=16) to validate() on the val geometries.

Separately, do the rigid split and the port overwrite in fp64: u = RA c (fp64) + ext(qd) (fp32 -> fp64), and likewise in field_T. This is exact and costs nothing. It removes fp32 rounding of large rigid parts, which the K product in the lattice PCG sees relative to a tiny deformation part.
proposals.addresses: The r2-y nbr_z failure (test-cell sensitivity 3.10%; interface 4.8% vs extension 1.0%; test-cell energy share 0.13%). Interface-only errors of 3.3-9.3%. Worst-direction mu 1.31-1.48, currently report-only. The step-2 validation metrics, which contain no mu.
proposals.expected_gain: mu_-F - 1 halved, so the interface error drops by ~sqrt(2) or more on dragged or glued loads. r2 y test-cell sensitivity 3.10% -> <= 2.5%. mu becomes a monitored step-2 quantity.
proposals.risk: Spending adversarial budget on faces could raise other classes' bank errors by a few percent. Ritz directions are network-specific and must be refreshed on each entry. The clamped factor adds memory, so use one factor at a time, as in prep.
proposals.cost: One extra fp32 factorization plus ~8 power iterations per entry for 1-2 faces: ~2-6 s per entry, about +5-10% step-2 wall time. No forward-pass change.
proposals.test:
(0) Verify the theory with diag_lat.py on r2 x/y using d2. Compute mu_-F for each gate configuration's shared face and e_q for the test cell's q_ref. Pass if sqrt((mu_-F - 1)(e_q - 1)) upper-bounds the interface-only error and ranks the loads (nbr_z worst).
Also rerun evalnet y with the fp64 wrapper. If nbr_z moves by more than 0.3 pt, precision is part of the failure.
(1) Step-1 r2 from d2, 5k steps with the clamped-face adversary versus 5k steps without.

Pass: mu_-F >= 2x lower; nbr_z y test-cell sensitivity <= 2.5%; x/y gate pass; bank classes within +5% of control.
(2) Carry into the next step-2 run and report mu_-F on the 20 val geometries at each EVAL.

proposals.title: Partition-of-unity, stiffness-weighted grid transfers (operator-dependent restriction, bounded PU prolongation; optional strong/fringe two-continuum coarse state)
proposals.component: coarse U-Net transfers (MGNO._restrict, _prolong, restrict_head, skip) and fastnet R/P matrices
proposals.mechanism:
Restriction: X_c(v) = sum_i t_iv rho_i X_i / sum_i t_iv rho_i, with rho_i = (D_i/median D)^kappa softplus(r_i) and kappa learnable, initialized at 0. This is the black-box-multigrid operator-dependent average, so coarse values represent the strong material and weak or fringe values do not pollute them.

Prolongation: P_iv = t_iv pi_iv / sum_v' t_iv' pi_iv', with pi_iv = exp(clip(g(gn_i, gl_v), +-log 4)) over the at most 8 coarse vertices of each fine node. This is an exact partition of unity, so constants are reproduced at every level, and linear fields too when pi = 1. A bounded amplitude (1 + 0.5 tanh) replaces the unbounded softplus w_i. Coarse corrections then stop creating spurious strain in near-rigid and bending (soft) modes and cannot amplify on unseen geometries.

Optional two-continuum variant (CEM-GMsFEM / GenEO, high-contrast media): each 33^3 and 17^3 vertex carries a strong copy and a weak copy (masks chi_s + chi_w = 1, F/2 extra channels), prolonged with chi-weights so the partition of unity is preserved. This gives the fringe its own long-wavelength coarse degrees of freedom. Use it only if the P3 oracle shows the fringe is not locally condensable.

Warm start: blend the old w_i prolongation with the partition-of-unity form, lambda initialized at 0.
proposals.addresses: Gain instability on unseen geometries (unbounded softplus prolongation, ~40 chained stages). Soft/near-rigid-mode mu. Fringe contamination of coarse states. Fringe modes that are non-local, if P3's oracle fails.
proposals.expected_gain: Modest at step 1 (<= 10% bank error, mu down 10-20%). Larger on held-out geometries: fewer macro/GRF blow-ups and faster first-entry recovery.
proposals.risk: The partition of unity removes the network's ability to switch off coarse corrections locally, e.g. at ports, which the current w_i may be doing; hence the bounded amplitude kept as a safety valve. The two-continuum variant adds 30-60% U-Net cost and parameters.
proposals.cost: Partition of unity plus rho: negligible (8 pair weights per fine node, geometry path once). Two-continuum: +30-60% U-Net compute and ~+0.15M parameters.
proposals.test:
(0) Free pre-check on d2: quantiles of rw[l][1] by node class (weak, strong, port) on r2 versus 0031-medium, dev_0000 and dev_0002. If weak-node or unseen-geometry values deviate by more than 2x from strong in-distribution values, proceed.
(1) Step-1 r2 A/B from d2 (10k): no worse than control on the bank, with mu reported.
(2) Step-2 arm (combined with P2 if P2 passed) versus the main-line checkpoints.

Pass: held-out macro/GRF bank errors >= 20% lower; max first-entry ADV ritz lower than control.

proposals.title: Island/near-mechanism-aware exact rigid split: partition of unity over material components, with diagonal-weighted rigid fit
proposals.component: wrapper (trainlib.Geo.field lines 139-147 and fastnet.field/field_T lines 203-214): the rigid split only
proposals.mechanism:
Material components: connect nodes through elements with vf > 1e-3, excluding connections made only by ghost faces or near-empty elements. A component tied to the rest only through the ghost penalty (gamma = 1e-4) or thin necks has relative rigid motions with energy ~gamma. These are near-mechanisms, giving pencil directions with very large mu, and the network does not reproduce rigid motions internally.

Split:
1. c_k = (RP_k^T W RP_k)^-1 RP_k^T W q on the component-k ports, with W = diag(D_p), so fringe port nodes (924 in FULL) do not steer the fit.
2. Take phi_k as a smooth partition of unity (graph-diffused component indicators, transitions placed inside weak or ghost-only regions, sum_k phi_k = 1).
3. u = net(q - sum_k phi_k(P) RP c_k) + sum_k phi_k RA c_k, then the port overwrite.

The split stays exact and linear: global rigid motions are reproduced exactly (sum phi = 1), per-island rigid motions are also reproduced exactly, and port values stay exact. With a single component it reduces to today's split (with D-weighting).
proposals.addresses: Catastrophic first-entry worst ratios (106, 280, 46) if they come from near-disconnected geometries. The fp32 interior-factorization failure seen in data prep (a near-singular geometry). The declared hard class 'slivers / nearly disconnected islands'. The lens's rigid-like modes.
proposals.expected_gain: Conditional. Where islands or necks exist, mu for those geometries drops by orders of magnitude and their bank errors approach the pool median. Otherwise no effect; the D-weighted fit alone is neutral to slightly positive.
proposals.risk: Detection thresholds. A partition-of-unity transition cutting through stiff material would inject strain; keep it in weak or ghost-only zones. Changes the network's input distribution, so it needs a fine-tune.
proposals.cost: Trivial: connected components once per geometry, plus a few extra rigid fits per q.
proposals.test:
(0) 10-minute check on all 206 geometries:
- component counts and neck sizes;
- the 8 smallest nonzero Ritz values of S via the Neumann factor, compared with the force-bank Rayleigh median of 1.8e-7;
- correlation with the ADV ritz_top at first entry in s2_full train.log and with per-geometry val errors at the 10k EVAL.

Proceed only if islands exist and their geometries are the outliers.
(1) Fine-tune on the worst such geometry, with and without the split, for 5k steps.

Pass: adversarial mu >= 5x lower; bank errors within the pool's interquartile range.

proposals.title: Bounded coefficient range: normalized, saturating geometry heads, after a blow-up diagnosis
proposals.component: geometry path heads (slot_head, fslot_head, slot_head_x, restrict_head, gate_head) and MGCache input clamps
proposals.mechanism:
Step 0, diagnosis on existing checkpoints (no training):
- For each zero-shot pair, compute the amplitude ratio ||u_hat-u*||_inf/||u*||_inf per node group (weak, port-adjacent, other).
- Split the error energy with diag_error.py (weak elements / GP / port elements / other; smooth vs rough).
- Measure the share of error energy in elements whose q-path coefficients (ab, fab, xab, rw) fall outside the training geometry's [p0.1, p99.9] range.

Change:
- Head input z = [LN(ge_e), LN(gn_i), slot_s, vf_e, rho_i]. LN is a LayerNorm over the Cg=64 embedding after each message-passing round. The raw scalars are re-appended so the absolute material level is not normalized away.
- Coefficients a = A*tanh(a_raw/A) and b likewise, per layer, head and a/b, for the element, GP-face and fringe heads. A = 2x the p99.9 of |coef| over the 148 training geometries under the current step-2 checkpoint, stored as fixed buffers. In-range values change by less than (x/A)^2/3: at most 8% at p99.9, and essentially nothing at the median.
- Transfer weights w = w_max*tanh(softplus(r)/w_max) + 1e-3. Gates stay 2*sigmoid.
- Input clamps: normalized moments clamp(M_1:/vol, -1, 1), since |xi^a eta^b zeta^c| <= 1 means valid values lie in [-1, 1]; ld clamped to [-12, 3].

Effect:
- Per hyperedge layer, ||I+T||_inf <= 1 + 27*H*A_a*A_b*max||W_h||, with the same bound for every geometry.
- Out-of-distribution features can at worst saturate at the training range. They can no longer drive the (1+eps)^36 runaway.
- The saturation fraction per geometry is logged as a free out-of-distribution score.

Two variants: G1a (tanh bounds and clamps only) keeps the warm start; G1b adds LN, for the next run from initialization.
proposals.addresses:
Mechanism B:
- FULL0020->dev_0002 macro 1745% / GRF 869%, about 40x the zero-parameter baseline (0.32-0.45).
- r1->heavy cuts 1.2e3-2.8e3x, against a baseline force ratio of 9-15.
- Step-2 first-entry worst ratios 106 and 280, above the baseline worst of 72-78.

In models.py the coefficients are 0.2*MLP with no normalization, and the transfer weights are softplus, unbounded above.
proposals.expected_gain:
Removes the heavy tail rather than lowering the mean. Estimates:
- First-entry worst ratio after 5k steps at or below about 10 (now 19-280 early).
- Maximum per-geometry val force error roughly halved.
- In-distribution class means within 5% of control.
proposals.risk:
Low.
- A box calibrated too tight clips legitimately large coefficients on thin or heavily cut geometries. If in-distribution error rises, raise A to 3x p99.9.
- LN breaks an exact warm start, so G1b is only for from-initialization runs.
proposals.cost: Less than 1% step time, no extra memory. Calibration pass (geometry path over 148 geometries) about 15 min. Step-0 diagnosis about 1 h GPU.
proposals.test:
(0) Diagnosis on four zero-shot pairs: r2->dev_0000, r2->0031 medium, FULL0020->dev_0002, r1->0031 heavy. Compare each with its self-evaluation, using 64 val directions per class. Mechanism B is confirmed if the amplitude ratio is at least 5, or at least 50% of the error energy sits in out-of-range-coefficient elements.

(1) Two arms, 10k more steps each from the step-2 checkpoint at LR 3e-4, same seeds and pool order:
- Arm A: unchanged.
- Arm B: with G1a.

Measure: zs_eval per class (mean, p90, max) on the 20 val geometries and the 12 training probes, and ADV ritz_top at first entry for entries during the run.

Pass: the maximum over val geometries of the force mean error is at most 0.6x arm A, and the median first-entry ritz is at most 0.7x arm A, with val and probe class means within +5% of A.

proposals.title: Coarse operators that depend on geometry and direction, fed by a multilevel geometry encoder
proposals.component: coarse U-Net of the q path, plus a new geometry U-Net in the geometry path
proposals.mechanism:
(a) Geometry U-Net:
- Restrict gn to 33^3 / 17^3 / 9^3 as now, then process each level with 2 residual blocks [conv3d 3x3x3 Cg->Cg on the dense grid with an activity-mask channel, LN, GELU].
- At 9^3, add a masked mean-pool global vector used as FiLM on all levels. Mean, not sum, so cells with 19k-430k DOFs are comparable.
- Decode by upsample-add back to fine nodes (gn += P(g^33)), so the fine alpha/beta also see cell-wide context such as whether this ligament is in the load path.

(b) Coarse hyperedge layers:
- At 33^3 and 17^3 (optionally 9^3), replace the first conv of both the down and up pair with a 27-slot stencil layer on the coarse vertex grid.
- Hyperedge = voxel i; slots d in {-1,0,1}^3, with inactive neighbours masked.
- Z_i^h = sum_d alpha_{i,d,h} X_{i+d};  X_{i+d} += beta_{i,d,h} W_h Z_i^h / deg.
- alpha, beta = bounded heads of [LN(g_i), LN(g_{i+d}), slot_d], with the G1 bounds.
- This is the same operator as the fine element layers (reuse sparse_layers.hyper, with hn = neighbourhood list). Coarse couplings then depend on direction and geometry: strong along a wall, none across a void or cut.

(c) Fine geometry message passing goes from 2 to 3 rounds with LN residual blocks.

New beta heads are zero-initialized, so a warm start reproduces the current function at step 0.
proposals.addresses:
The transfer failure is concentrated in the soft, global classes:
- r2->0031 medium: force 306%, support 353%, against face 66% and GRF 41%.
- r2->dev_0000: force 407% (max 2151%), against macro 14% and GRF 9%.
- r2->0031 heavy: force 107%, against macro 7%.

Soft directions (Rayleigh 1.8e-7 vs 1e-4) are carried by the coarse path. Its only geometry dependence today is per-voxel gates (the same in every direction) and scalar transfer weights computed from averaged fine features.
proposals.expected_gain: Estimated 15-30% lower held-out force, support and adversarial errors and worst-direction mu. A smaller train-val gap in force/support. May also move the step-1 worst mu (1.3-1.5).
proposals.risk:
- More geometry-dependent coefficients mean more exposure to out-of-distribution features; always combine with G1.
- At 17^3 and 9^3 a coarse voxel can hold two disconnected shell sheets: the Schwarz-P channel is 0.3-0.5 of a cell, a 9^3 voxel is 1/8 of a cell. One coarse state cannot separate them. Measure first the fraction of coarse voxels whose active fine nodes form more than one connected component.
- Memory +5-8%.
proposals.cost:
- One coarse hyperedge layer at 33^3 costs about one fine element layer (active vertices are about E); at 17^3 about 1/8 of that. In total about +2.5 layer-equivalents on top of the 24 layers today, so roughly +8-10% step time (0.229 -> about 0.25 s) and +1-2 GB at batch 16.
- Geometry U-Net: about 10 GFLOP forward per step, +1-2%.
- About +0.3 M parameters.
proposals.test:
Multi-component voxel fraction first.

Then two step-2 arms from the same initialization, both with G1a, 20k steps, same seeds:
- Control.
- G2.

Measure:
- zs_eval per class mean and p90 on the 20 val geometries.
- Train-probe gap.
- Worst-direction mu on 5 val geometries (adversarial k=16, 8 iterations, Neumann factor).
- Lattice gate with evalnet.py on one held-out cut geometry, with the neighbour set to its own family FULL parent, plus the diag_lat.py decomposition.

Pass: val force and support means at least 15% lower, worst mu lower on at least 4 of 5 val geometries, lattice compliance and sensitivity not worse, step time at most +15%.

proposals.title: Input features that mean the same thing in every geometry: dimensionless, local, fixed references
proposals.component: geometry path inputs (MGCache efeat/nfeat) and the weak/fringe masks
proposals.mechanism:
(a) Fixed stiffness reference:
- rho_i = log(||d3_i|| / d_full_i), where d_full_i = ||sum_{e contains i} K_e^full[s,s]||_F and K_e^full = sum_m M_m^full T_m, using full-cube moments (a constant per slot type).
- d_full depends only on which elements around i are active. rho_i is the material fraction node i sees, with the same meaning in every geometry, and it does not depend on E.
- It replaces log(d3/median(d3)).

(b) Continuous weakness:
- w_i = sigmoid((log 0.01 - rho_i)/0.5) becomes an input feature.
- The fringe layers run on a superset mask (rho < log 0.05) with messages scaled by the element's maximum w. The fringe-layer domain then no longer jumps when the geometry's median moves the 1% threshold.

(c) Moment features:
- clamp(M_1:/vol, -1, 1) * s(vf), with s = vf/(vf + 1e-3), so noise-dominated sliver moments do not enter at full weight.
- Keep vf and log vf.

(d) Local frame instead of absolute position:
- Drop sin/cos(2*pi*g/64).
- Add: signed distance to the cut plane (n.x - offset)/h, clipped to +-6 elements (0 plus a flag for FULL cells); distances to the 6 box planes, clipped to 6 elements; graph hop distance to the nearest port (multi-source BFS on element adjacency, clipped at 8).

(e) Rollout that keeps the warm start: add the new columns with zero-initialized input weights first, then remove the old ones in a second arm.
proposals.addresses:
FULL0020->FULL0031 (similar thickness) transfers at 8.5%; FULL0020->dev_0002 (different thickness) fails at 2236%, with the same absolute coordinates in both. The failure follows thickness, and so do three current inputs: the median-referenced diag feature, the 1%-of-median weak flag, and the fringe-layer domains derived from it.

Absolute coordinates tie the rules to position in the cell rather than to the cut and box frame, which changes with depth rv in [0, 1] and angle theta.
proposals.expected_gain: Estimated 10-25% lower val errors, or a smaller train-val gap. First-entry ratios should fall faster, and fringe treatment should be consistent across thickness (visible in the stress test).
proposals.risk:
Low to moderate.
- Drops the TPMS-phase information in absolute coordinates; the moments carry the local shape, so the loss should be small.
- Changing the weak/fringe definitions changes where the MGNO2 fringe layers act, so expect 2-5k steps of re-learning.
proposals.cost: Features are built once per geometry in milliseconds (BFS is 8 sparse matvecs; d_full comes from 27 constants). No step-time change.

proposals.title: Cubic-group (O_h) augmentation on the fly by index permutation, with optional group-averaged inference
proposals.component: trainer (train2 Slot / Geo.field wrapper) and inference (fastnet)
proposals.mechanism:
Group action. For g in O_h: P_g permutes the 65^3 grid nodes (axis permutation plus flips i_a -> 64-i_a), and R_g is the signed permutation of the displacement components; T_g = P_g kron R_g.

The rotated geometry's inputs are exact index images. V01 showed cells, nodes, box nodes and GP faces are exact permutation images with a single node ordering, and energies agree to 1e-7.
- Moments: M_abc -> sign * M_pi(abc), with sign = (-1) to the power of the exponents of flipped axes.
- elem_nodes are re-sorted into the canonical slot order of the rotated frame.
- The GP-face axis is permuted.
- Flags and diag3 norms are permuted.

Forward pass: u_hat = T_g^T N(g.geo, T_g q_d) + R_A c, with port values overwritten as now. Energy and sensitivity are computed in the base frame with the base K and dM, so no teacher data or labels change.

On each slot entry, draw g uniformly (identity with p = 0.25) and build the MGCache of g.geo, replacing the base cache during that residency.

Optional inference: E_G = (1/m) sum_{g in G_m} T_g^T E_hat(g.geo) T_g. It is still linear, with exact ports and rigid part. By convexity:
e(E_G q) - e* = ||mean d_g||_K^2 = mean ||d_g||_K^2 - mean ||d_g - d_bar||_K^2 <= mean (e_g - e*).
So it is never worse than the average member.
proposals.addresses:
Coverage: the user's scope is cut angle 0-45 deg in one plane, with other orientations by rotation, and 28 thickness fields. Augmentation turns 148 geometries into 148x48 views with no solves and no memory. Today the encoder sees moments in the global frame and free per-slot embeddings, so nothing ties the '+x' rule to the '+y' rule.

History: rotation augmentation improved held-out cut cells from 0.64 to 0.41 (EquiModel).
proposals.expected_gain:
Estimates:
- Rotated val errors go from (likely) several-fold worse to within 1.2x of unrotated.
- 10-20% on unrotated held-out families through regularization.
- Group-averaged inference with m = 4 gives a further 5-15% lower energy error.
proposals.risk:
- F = 32 capacity is shared across orientations: a few percent in-distribution, or more steps.
- Moment and slot maps can be implemented wrong. Guard with a unit test: K_e rebuilt from permuted moments equals the permuted K_e to 1e-12 for 5 elements and 5 group elements.
- Low overall.
proposals.cost: About 1 day of engineering. +1-3 s per slot entry (cache build), about +2-4% wall time at swap_every = 300. No per-step cost. Group-averaged inference costs m times the inference and encoding.
proposals.test:
(0) Now, before any training:
- Evaluate the step-2 checkpoint on the 20 val geometries under 3 random non-identity g, using a rotation wrapper around zs_eval.
- Check in SPLIT.json that every *_rot* packet is in the same split as its base; otherwise val is leaking.

(1) Augmentation arm vs control, 20k steps. Measure val per class, unrotated and rotated, and the equivariance gap delta = mean |e_hat(g.geo, T_g q) - e_hat(geo, q)| / e_hat.

Pass: rotated val at most 1.2x unrotated, unrotated val not worse than +5%, delta < 1%.

(2) Group-averaged inference with m = 4 on val: report the gain over the mean member (guaranteed at least 0).

proposals.title: Label-free blow-up monitor: a certified lower bound on the error from the readout residual
proposals.component: inference and trainer monitor only; it never modifies the field
proposals.mechanism:
The readout already computes r = K u_hat. With exact port values, d = u_hat - u* lives on the interior and K_II d = r_I, so ||d||_K^2 = r_I^T K_II^-1 r_I = e_hat - e*.

Lower bound: for any basis V on I, LB = b^T G^-1 b with b = V^T r_I and G = V^T K_II V gives LB <= ||d||_K^2. Use the block-Jacobi Krylov basis v1 = D^-1 r_I, v_{k+1} = D^-1 K_II v_k (D = the 3x3 diagonal blocks already in NETDATA), m = 8-16. This certifies mu_q - 1 >= LB/(e_hat - LB).

Baseline test: e_GL(q) from the graph-harmonic lift (ops.GraphLift) is also an upper bound on e*. So e_hat > e_GL certifies 'worse than the zero-parameter baseline'.

The G1 saturation fraction adds a free encoder-side score.

Uses:
1. Deployment: probe each new cell with 32 macro + 32 GRF directions, plus the cell's actual lattice port data q. Flag it if the median LB ratio exceeds 5%, or if the baseline test fails.
2. Training curriculum: re-enter geometries with high LB more often, and add the highest-LB probe directions to the adversarial pool when no Neumann factor is available.
3. Optional rescue: a few hundred steps of per-geometry adaptation with the same label-free log e_hat loss on the flagged cell's actual q. K appears only in the loss.

The Krylov steps are a residual iteration, but only inside the monitor. The field never uses them; if it did, this would be fallback A.
proposals.addresses:
There is no teacher at deployment, yet zero-shot failures reach 1e2-1e3x. Because S_hat >= S, blow-ups are always 'too stiff' and can be certified from below.

The route-2 equilibrated certificate (efficiency 1.10-1.15) exists but costs 228 s of CPU per cell.
proposals.expected_gain: Near-certain detection of mechanism-B blow-ups, which are rough or local errors that the Jacobi-Krylov basis captures quickly, in about 20-50 ms per cell. Weaker for smooth global errors in soft directions, where LB efficiency may be 10-30%.
proposals.risk:
- False negatives on smooth errors.
- The threshold needs calibration.
- The rescue path costs about 1 min per flagged cell: fine as an exception, too slow for routine design iterations.
proposals.cost: m fp64 K products per probe batch (milliseconds each). One sparse Laplacian factorization per cell for the optional GraphLift test (monitor only).
proposals.test:
Pairs:
- Zero-shot, with exact labels: r2->0031 medium/heavy, r2->dev_0000, FULL0020->dev_0002, FULL0020->0031, r1->0031 / dev_0000.
- Their self-evaluations.

On these, compute LB_16/(e_hat - LB_16) against the true mu-1 per val direction and class.

Pass:
- every pair with a true force mean error above 50% is flagged using the macro+GRF probes alone;
- no self-evaluation (true error about 2%) is flagged;
- Spearman >= 0.7 between the per-geometry median LB ratio and the true force error across the step-2 model's 20 val geometries.

Report the LB/true efficiency per class.

proposals.title: Thickness-jitter geometries without new labels, with soft directions from the entry factorization
proposals.component: sampling and trainer (train2 slot entry), plus the geometry cache
proposals.mechanism:
On slot entry, with p = 0.5:
- Replace the 8 corner thicknesses tau with tau + dtau, |dtau|_inf <= Delta (0.03-0.05 on the tau range [0.175, 0.699]).
- Recompute moments on the geometry's fixed cell set with C.moments(taus), the same routine used for the dK/dtau differences (0.2-1 s).
- Reassemble K (moments times Tm plus the tau-independent GP base).
- Rebuild diag3, weak, efeat, nfeat and the fringe masks.
- Shrink dtau if any active element's vf drops below the base geometry's minimum.

Directions:
1. The base banks: macro and GRF stay exactly valid; force, support and face stay nearly soft.
2. Fresh force directions q = S_tau^+ f (prep_data generators) and adversarial directions, both from the fp32 Neumann factor that adversarial_on_load already builds on entry.

Loss: log e_hat only. It is scale-invariant (grad log e_hat(cq) = grad log e_hat(q)), so no exact normalization is needed. The sensitivity loss is off for jittered slots. Errors are reported only on the fresh force q, whose exact energy f^T q comes from the same solve.
proposals.addresses: Training has only 28 distinct thickness fields (families) in an 8-D tau space, and thickness is the axis where transfer breaks (FULL->FULL: similar thickness 8.5%, different thickness 2236%). Val and test families are unseen tau fields. The design loop also moves tau continuously, so E_hat(tau) must be smooth.
proposals.expected_gain: Estimated 10-25% lower val errors on unseen families and a smoother E_hat in tau, with no extra teacher preparation and no disk.
proposals.risk:
- The fixed cell set truncates thickening at the active-set boundary (flat facets), and thinning leaves near-empty active elements. This is a mild distribution shift, controlled by Delta and the vf rule.
- No sensitivity supervision on jittered slots.
- K values are held twice briefly on entry.
proposals.cost: +2-4 s per entry (moments, assembly, cache, about 128 extra Neumann solves), about +3-5% wall time. No change to step time or steady-state memory.

proposals.title: Stiffness-weighted aggregation and bounded affine extrapolation at weak (fictitious) nodes
proposals.component: q-path fine and fringe hyperedge layers, plus a final output stage for weak nodes
proposals.mechanism:
(a) Stiffness-share aggregation:
- Replace dX_i = (1/deg_i) sum_{e contains i} Y_{e,i} with dX_i = sum_e pi_{e,i} Y_{e,i}.
- pi_{e,i} = kappa_{e,i} / sum_{e'} kappa_{e',i}, with kappa_{e,i} = ||K_e[s,s]||_F + eps (element diagonal block from moments times templates); for GP-face hyperedges kappa = gamma*||G_f[s,s]||.
- This is the split a Jacobi step uses. A fringe node then follows its material-carrying elements instead of an equal vote of near-empty ones.
- These are geometry-only scalars, the same kind of input as the diag3 features, and involve no solve.

(b) Output stage for nodes with weakness w_i > 0 (w from G3):
- u_i <- (1 - w_i k_i) u_i^net + w_i k_i sum_{j in S(i)} c_ij u_j^net.
- S(i) = strong nodes of the elements and GP-face neighbours around i.
- c_i = Omega_i P_i^T (P_i Omega_i P_i^T + lambda I)^-1 e_1, with P_i = [1; (x_j - x_i)/h] (4 x |S_i|). This is a moving-least-squares extrapolation that reproduces affine fields exactly, and therefore rigid motions.
- Omega = diag(softplus(head)) and gate k_i = sigmoid(head) are both bounded; lambda bounds ||c_i||_1.
- Still linear in q, with geometry-only 4x4 solves at encode time. This is the aggregated finite element (AgFEM) device that makes cut discretizations robust to where the cut falls.
proposals.addresses:
- Weak nodes are 18-22% of all nodes.
- Step-1 block diagnosis: 36% of force-direction error energy is in the GP term, and 45% of body error is in weak elements.
- Loads on fringe nodes inflate sensitivity error 2-4x in the stress test (FULL 8.2-8.5%, r2 5.3-6.7%).
- The energy loss gives weak-node errors less than 1% of median stiffness weight, so trained networks can leave large values there cheaply and pay when a new geometry makes those nodes stiffer.
proposals.expected_gain: Conditional on the G1 diagnosis. Estimated -30% error energy in GP plus weak elements on held-out geometries, -30% stress-test sensitivity error, small effect on bank means.
proposals.risk:
Moderate.
- The exact GP fictitious field is closer to a quadratic continuation, so an affine prior can bias it; the gate k lets the network override.
- Part (a) changes the function the warm start computes, so it needs re-training.
proposals.cost: Part (a) is free (weights precomputed). Part (b) is one sparse matrix per geometry (weak nodes x about 20-60 neighbours), under 1% time.

proposals.title: Geometry-stationary pool sampler: fast cycling with prefetch, hard-geometry mining with a uniform floor, stratified batches, weight EMA, correct generalization probes
proposals.component: trainer / sampling (train2.py)
proposals.mechanism: (a) swap_every 300 -> 25, with 2 resident geometries plus 1 prefetched slot (pinned host tensors loaded from slots/<case>.pt by a background thread and copied non_blocking on a side CUDA stream). One pass over the 148 geometries then takes 3.7k steps (about 16 passes in 60k) instead of 44.4k. (b) Choose the next geometry with p_g = 0.5/N + 0.5 * Lbar_g / sum Lbar, capped at 4/N. Lbar_g is an EMA over visits of the geometry's mean log e_hat, initialised by its first visit. The last 10% of steps use uniform order (consolidation). (c) Fixed class counts per batch (e.g. 4 force, 3 face, 2 support, 2 macro, 2 grf, 3 adv) instead of multinomial draws, to reduce gradient variance. (d) Weight EMA with decay 0.9997 (horizon about one pass), saved beside last/best. Select checkpoints by the maximum over val geometries of the p90 energy error (force/support/face) plus sensitivity p90, not by the max of class means. (e) LRU cap on host-resident slots, reloading from slot_cache. (f) Every 20k steps evaluate the val banks of all 148 training geometries (about 5 min) and log steps-since-last-visit, so the train vs held-out gap is not biased by forgetting (probes are currently order[:12]). (g) LR: keep the 1e-3 peak for this phase, since the loss was 0.82 at step 50, far from any optimum. Any continuation of a converged step-2 model must use a peak <= 3e-4 with a control arm of the same length (the warm-start lesson).
proposals.addresses: The 44.4k-step pass (1.35 passes in 60k, about 300 steps per visit at LR 1e-3) and the recency bias of the cosine tail (last 15k steps cover about 50 geometries). Also the forgetting-biased probe set (order[:12]), catastrophic first-entry worst ratios (106, 280, 46, ...), and the host-RAM growth to 168 slots.
proposals.expected_gain: Held-out (20 val geometries) mean and p90 energy error 20-40% lower at equal steps. The max/median error spread across geometries roughly halved. A valid train vs held-out gap for the user's data-sufficiency decision. Estimates; test 0 confirms or refutes the premise at no cost.
proposals.risk: I/O stalls if prefetch falls behind (fallback: synchronous swap of about 0.5-1 s, 5-10% overhead). Mining can over-focus on irreducibly hard slivers (hence the cap and the uniform final phase). The EMA lags early in training. GPU memory is 28.4 of 31.4 GB, so the prefetch slot must replace a resident one.
proposals.cost: About half a day of code. Runtime overhead <= 5% with prefetch. No new data. Full-training-set evaluation about 5 min every 20k steps.
proposals.test: Test 0 (now, zero cost): evaluate the running job's 10k and 20k checkpoints on the val banks of every training geometry visited so far. Compute Spearman rho(error, steps since last visit) and the ratio of early-visited to recently-visited geometry error. Forgetting is confirmed if rho > 0.4 or the ratio > 1.5. Test 1: 20k steps of P1 against the current trainer, same d2 init and same schedule (compare at equal steps and at equal wall time). Pass if held-out force/support/face mean and p90 are >= 20% lower, sensitivity mean is not worse, rho < 0.2, and max/median over training geometries <= 3. Then run evalnet (consistent loads) on 2 held-out val-family geometries, each with its own family's FULL cell as the exact neighbour.

proposals.title: Lattice-consistent q classes: traction-consistent loads, stiffness-proportional supports, and an exact glued-neighbour class
proposals.component: sampling / data (prep_geo.py and prep_data.py generators; train mix)
proposals.mechanism: (a) force_c / face_c: nodal load f_i = integral over (Gamma intersect material) of t(x) N_i(x) dA. t is a random smooth traction (the existing plane-wave/patch generators, evaluated at face quadrature points inside material, reusing the deployed consistent-gate quadrature with random t instead of unit t). force_c loads all faces (10% also add a cut-surface traction). face_c loads one face, projected to be self-equilibrated. A facenet variant applies a net force balanced by (b). (b) support_c: spring k_i = alpha * diag(K)_ii with alpha log-uniform in [0.3, 3] on one face, replacing alpha * mean diagonal, so fringe nodes get weak springs as with a real glued neighbour. (c) glue: two-cell exact solve at prep. The geometry is glued by absolute node position (as in lattice3) to its family's FULL parent at a random box face that has material. The neighbour's far face is clamped (50%) or on springs (50%). Random smooth consistent tractions (random directions, net force allowed) go on random faces of either cell; 25% load only the neighbour, which covers dragged states. One sparse factorization of the combined K, then 64-96 solves. The solve returns the test-cell field u_t, so its port data q_t (rigid part removed), exact energy u_t'K_t u_t, reaction S q_t = (K_t u_t)_P and exact sensitivities -u_t'K'_c u_t all come free, with no test-cell interior factorization. The gate's 6 unit loads are never used. Suggested mix: force (nodal) 5, force_c 15, face_c 15, support_c 10, glue 20, macro 10, grf 10, adv 15. Because the log loss is scale-invariant, normalization is needed only for reporting.
proposals.addresses: Extension-only sensitivity error at exact lattice port data of 5.3-9.9%, against 0.6-1.5% on the banks. Training dominated by uniform-nodal-type loads that the gate abandoned because they inflate error 2-4x. Support springs that clamp fringe nodes. Weak coverage of the dragged state (nbr_facex0_z, 0.13% energy share). Consistent with the step-1 finding that coverage drove most gains.
proposals.expected_gain: Extension-only errors at lattice data 30-50% lower. r2 y gate test-cell sensitivity 3.10% -> <= 2.5%. Held-out gate errors closer to training-geometry errors. The stress test (uniform nodal) may lose about 0.5 pt, mitigated by keeping 5% nodal loads.
proposals.risk: Configuration leakage on training geometries, since the parent-neighbour arrangement matches the gate; decisive numbers must come from held-out families. The combined-system factorization for the largest geometries (up to about 700k DOFs) needs the GPU free; skip geometries above a DOF limit and report which. The stress test may regress.
proposals.cost: About 1 day of generator code. Re-prep: (a) and (b) reuse the existing Neumann/spring factorizations (about 40-60 s per geometry); (c) adds one combined factorization (about 20-40 s). Roughly 3-4 GPU hours for 168 geometries, which cannot overlap with training (28.4 GB in use). Disk +30-50%.
proposals.test: Step-1 test first, because its numbers are known. Regenerate r2's banks with (a)-(c), warm-start from d2 and train 10k steps at 3e-4: arm P2 (new mix) against a control with the old mix and the same steps (as arm e). Measure diag_lat extension-only and interface errors for r2 x and y, the evalnet gate (consistent) and stress test, and the old-bank val errors. Pass if the median extension-only error over the 12 gate loads is >= 30% lower than control, gate test-cell sensitivity <= 2.5% in both configs, old-bank val errors are not worse by more than 10% relative, and the stress test is not worse by more than 1 pt. Then in step 2: the held-out gate on val-family geometries.

proposals.title: Exact reaction bank F = S Q, a subspace-Ritz (dual-norm) tail loss, and a factorization-free bank-span adversary
proposals.component: loss + sampling + data (trainlib._Energy -> batch Gram; train2 loss; prep saves F)
proposals.mechanism: Store F = S q for every bank vector: normalize() already computes C.apply(q) = S q and throws it away, and for the glue class F = (K_t u_t)_P. At each step, replace the diagonal energy with the batch Gram G_hat = U'KU (B x B). KU is already formed inside _Energy, and the backward is dL/dU = KU (g + g'). The exact Gram is G = Q'F in fp64. Compute the Ritz values lambda_i of the pencil (G_hat, G) via Cholesky of G with an eigenvalue floor of 1e-3 * lambda_max(G); lambda_i >= 1 because S_hat >= S. Loss: L = mean_b log G_hat_bb + w_T * tau * log sum_i exp(log lambda_i / tau) (smooth max, tau = 0.1, w_T about 0.3) + sensitivity term. Interpretation: sum_i (lambda_i - 1)^2 = ||G^-1/2 (G_hat - G) G^-1/2||_F^2 = sum_j ||P_B D v_j||^2 over an S-orthonormal basis v_j of the batch span. That is the reaction residual (S_hat - S) q in the dual (S^-1) norm, projected on the batch span, obtained with no adjoint pass and no solve. The off-diagonals G_hat_ab - G_ab = w_a'K w_b are the correlated (systematic) error components that the diagonal loss never sees. Bank-span adversary: for each resident geometry, every ~200 of its steps, take R = 256 bank vectors, compute U_R = E_hat Q_R without grad, G_hat_R = U_R'K U_R and G_R = Q_R'F_R. The top 8 generalized eigenvectors give x_j = Q_R c_j with exact S x_j = F_R c_j. They fill half the adversarial share and enter the Ritz loss with exact Gram entries. Cross terms against full-space adversarial vectors are also exact: x_adv'F_b. The top Ritz value mu_bank is a worst realistic-direction metric that needs no factorization, including on held-out val banks. The full adjoint dual norm ||S_hat q - f||^2_{S^+} is not proposed now: it needs double backward through the custom sparse layers (about 2-3x step cost).
proposals.addresses: Interface-only errors of 3.3-9.3%, explained by the bound sqrt((mu-1) eps) with mu-1 = 0.31-0.48. Worst direction mu 1.31-1.48. The fact that mean log e is blind to the tail. Catastrophic tails on new geometries (entry ratios 4.7-280). This is the 'loss on S_hat q vs S q in a dual norm' made computable.
proposals.expected_gain: mu_bank - 1 roughly halved. Interface-only errors about 30% lower. r2 y gate test-cell sensitivity 3.10% -> about 2.3-2.6%. Modest drop in full-space mu (1.31 -> about 1.2). All estimates to be confirmed by the step-1 test.
proposals.risk: An ill-conditioned G amplifies fp32 errors in G_hat (about 5e-6 relative x 1/lambda_min(G)), which is why the floor is needed. The smooth-max may trade mean for tail, so sweep w_T and watch bank means. F requires a prep pass. The bank-span adversary only finds combinations of realistic loads; P5 keeps covering fringe-local modes.
proposals.cost: F is the same size as the q banks (about 256 MB per geometry for the train split in fp32; resident on GPU for 2-3 slots, or gathered per batch from host). Prep: interior factorization + 3200 S-applies, about 25 s per geometry (about 70 min for 168; free if merged with the P2 re-prep). Per-step compute is negligible (16 x 16 eigh). Bank-span refresh is about 1 s per 200 steps (< 2%).
proposals.test: Step-1 test on r2: warm start from d2, 10k steps at 3e-4, arms control / P3 (w_T = 0.3) / P3 (w_T = 1.0). Measure mu_bank on the val bank, full-space mu (train1-style power iteration with k = 8 and 10 iterations), diag_lat interface-only error per load, and the evalnet gate. Pass if the median interface-only error is >= 30% lower, nbr_facex0_z test-cell sensitivity <= 2.5%, and bank val means are not worse by more than 5% relative. In step 2, report mu_bank on all 20 held-out geometries at every evaluation.

proposals.title: Sensitivity term rebalanced to the gate: smooth-L1 relative error, with optional finer regional labels
proposals.component: loss (train1/train2 sensitivity term; optional prep labels)
proposals.mechanism: Currently L_s = mean_b ||s_hat - s||^2 / ||s||^2, which near convergence is about c^2 eps with c about 0.07 (sensitivity error about 1% at eps about 0.02), i.e. about 0.5% of the gradient. Replace it with L_s = mean_b sqrt(rho_b^2 + delta^2), where rho_b = ||s_hat_b - s_b|| / ||s_b|| and delta = 0.003. Its gradient is about (c / (2 sqrt eps)) grad eps, about 25% of the energy gradient at sw = 1, and it keeps constant pressure as errors fall, which suits a max-type 3% gate. Optionally add CVaR_25% over the batch. Optional richer labels: 64 regional values (8 corners x 8 octants of the element-wise sensitivity density), computed in the same prep pass since sens(C, q) already forms the exact fields. They constrain the field error near the surface, where 8 trilinear-weighted sums can cancel. The glue class (P2) supplies these labels at lattice data.
proposals.addresses: Sensitivity is the binding gate metric (test cell 2.58% / 3.10%, against compliance 1.3-1.5% for r2 d2). The squared sensitivity term's gradient share is about 0.5%. Step-1 evidence: sensitivity supervision moved r1 x from 5.6% to 3.4%.
proposals.expected_gain: Gate test-cell sensitivity 15-25% lower (3.10% -> about 2.4-2.6%) at <= 10% relative energy cost.
proposals.risk: The 8-scalar functional can be matched by cancellation while fields stay wrong. Energy error may rise. Sensitivity is supervised only on labelled classes (not adversarial directions).
proposals.cost: About 10 lines, config only. Octant labels need the re-prep.
proposals.test: On r2: warm start from d2, 10k steps at 3e-4, arms squared sw = 1 (control), smooth-L1 sw = 1, smooth-L1 sw = 2. Run the evalnet gate (consistent and stress) and bank val. Pass if gate test-cell sensitivity <= 2.5% in both configs, compliance is not worse, and bank energy error rises by at most 10% relative. If it passes, bundle into step-2 run v2 (config only).

proposals.title: Persistent, warm-started, soft-seeded full-space adversary, with held-out tail monitoring
proposals.component: sampling / trainer (train2.adversarial_on_load, trainlib.adversarial)
proposals.mechanism: Keep a per-geometry host buffer of up to 32 vectors across visits. Refresh with block power iteration (k = 16, 4 iterations) started from [top 8 of the buffer, 8 force/face bank vectors] instead of a random block; seeding with soft-subspace directions follows DESIGN_operator-learning section 6.3. Refresh on the first visit, then when Lbar_g stagnates or every ~15k steps. Keep the budget <= 8% of wall time, since each refresh needs an fp32 Neumann factorization (about 10 s). The 15% adversarial share splits into 7% full-space and 8% bank-span (P3). The cross terms x_adv'F_b enter P3's pencil exactly. At each evaluation, compute zero-shot full-space mu on 5 held-out geometries (Neumann factorization + 10 iterations each).
proposals.addresses: Stale 8-vector sets (4 iterations from a random start, overwritten at every entry, against step 1's accumulated 256). First-entry ratios 106-280. Fringe-local modes behind the stress-test sensitivity of 5.3-8.5%. No held-out tail metric during step 2.
proposals.expected_gain: Held-out full-space mu 2-5x lower at the same step than with the entry-only adversary. Stress-test sensitivity 1-2 pt lower. Bank means unchanged.
proposals.risk: Wall-time budget. The approximate fp32 Neumann normalization gives a constant offset in log e, which does not affect the gradient. Over-emphasis on fringe modes the gate does not use (hence the split with P3).
proposals.cost: Small code change. <= 8% wall time. About 3 MB of host memory per geometry.
proposals.test: Inside the P1 run: arm with persistent/seeded buffers against entry-only random-start, both to 20k steps. Measure full-space mu on 5 held-out geometries and the bank means. Pass if median held-out mu <= 0.5x the entry-only arm and bank means are within 5%. Also run the stress test on one held-out geometry.

proposals.title: Geometry multiplication for the data-sufficiency gap: exact O_h augmentation, label-light geometries, on-the-fly macro/GRF
proposals.component: sampling / data
proposals.mechanism: (a) Apply one of the 48 signed permutations of the 65^3 grid to a whole slot. This covers the node index map, DOF component permutation and signs for K (exact, no re-assembly, which avoids the Kuhn-split re-integration asymmetry), moments via exact linear transforms of x^a y^b z^c (binomial for reflections), gp_face axes, node flags, sensitivity corners and the q/F banks. No new solves. Cut planes that span 0-45 deg in one plane then cover the other orientations, as in the user's scope. (b) Label-light new geometries from the generator (families.py): assembly + fp32 Neumann factorization for force_c/face_c directions only, with no interior factorization, no exact normalization (log loss is scale-invariant) and no sensitivity labels; these train the energy loss only. (c) Generate macro/GRF directions on the fly without a teacher, instead of drawing from 512 fixed vectors. Trigger (a)/(b) only if P1's valid measurement shows held-out / train-geometry error > 1.5.
proposals.addresses: Zero-shot blow-ups (100-2000x), i.e. limited geometry diversity. The train vs held-out gap the user wants to judge data sufficiency by. The planned rotation coverage (deferred to round 2). Overfitting to fixed macro/GRF banks.
proposals.expected_gain: Conditional: reduces the gap if it is data-limited. Rotated variants reach within 1.2x of unrotated error. (b) costs about 20-30 s of GPU per new geometry against about 70 s for full prep.
proposals.risk: Bugs in the moment transform; check against re-integration on the existing *_rotswapxy / *_rotinvert packets. The non-equivariant network (sin/cos coordinates, axis-specific kernels) must learn 48 orientations, a capacity question. Energy-only geometries dilute sensitivity supervision.
proposals.cost: About 1 day of code for (a). About 1 s of permutation work per visit. (b) about 20-30 s of GPU per geometry. (c) negligible.
proposals.test: Test 0 (now): run the current model zero-shot on rotated packets (*_rotswapxy / *_rotinvert) against their unrotated counterparts, comparing bank val energy and sensitivity; this measures orientation sensitivity. After adding (a): pass if the rotated/unrotated error ratio <= 1.2 and held-out unrotated error is not worse. For (b): add N label-light geometries only after P1's gap measurement, and require the held-out gap to shrink by >= 25%.

proposals.title: Cubic-group (O_h, 48 elements) augmentation by transforming parameters and features instead of the geometry (exact on the fixed grid, no new data)
proposals.component: trainer + model views (models.py MGNO/MGNO2 forward gets a group-element argument); geometry path feature transform; optional inference symmetrization
proposals.mechanism:
What it relies on. For h in O_h (a signed permutation R_h of the axes about the cell centre), the 65^3/33^3/17^3/9^3 grids map onto themselves. h.g is a legal family member: the Schwarz-P level set is O_h-invariant, the corner taus permute and the cut normal rotates. Most MGNO components are permutation-equivariant: index_add message passing, the element and GP-face hyperedge patterns, the trilinear transfers, the masks, deg, and the least-squares rigid split on an invariant port set. So E_theta(h.g) = P_h E_{theta_h}(g) P_h^T, where theta_h is a view of theta built as follows.
- Element slots: slot <- slot[pi_h], with pi_h taken from the local offsets o in {0,1,2}^3, o -> R_h(o-1)+1.
- GP-face slots: the 27-node face stencil is {owner middle layer, face layer, neighbour middle layer}. That is a symmetric node set, so a flip along the face axis only reverses the layer blocks and swaps the owner/neighbour inputs of face_in. The in-plane (b,d) indices transform with R_h and the axis one-hot is permuted.
- W_in <- R_h^T W_in and W_out <- W_out R_h; conv3d kernels are spatially flipped or transposed.
- Features transform exactly. The moment ratios are monomials x^a y^b z^c in centred local coordinates (xi in [-1,1], polyref_torch_fast), so T_h is a 125x125 signed permutation. sin/cos(2 pi g) get sign flips and permutations. vf, log vf, the flags and log|diag3| are invariant.
Training: draw h at random each step. K, the banks, the corner sensitivities, the rigid split and the cached sparse patterns are the original geometry's, so nothing new is stored or rebuilt. Inference: the identity view, or an average over views (L2). Precedents: Lie-point symmetry augmentation (Brandstetter et al., ICML 2022, arXiv:2202.07643); O_h 3D G-CNNs (Winkels & Cohen, MIDL 2018, arXiv:1804.04656). Equivariance by construction (Grega et al., ICLR 2024, arXiv:2401.16914; RESEARCH.md 6.5) stays the later upgrade.
proposals.addresses: The step-2 generalization gap: 148 geometries in 28 families, with zero-shot force errors of 107-407% on unseen cut families. The user scope says 'other cut orientations by rotation augmentation', which is not implemented today, so every rotated orientation is a zero-shot geometry. It also removes the net's orientation-specific parameters: slot/fslot embeddings, W_in/W_out, conv kernels, sin/cos coordinates, face owner order.
proposals.expected_gain: 48x more geometric diversity per geometry, with no extra data, memory or disk. Literature: about 10x data efficiency for O_h-equivariant 3D CNNs, and lower data needs for equivariant elasticity GNNs. Project evidence: rotation augmentation reduced the held-out cut-cell error from 0.64 to 0.41 (RESEARCH.md 6.4). Expected: rotated-view errors drop from catastrophic to near the identity-view level, and the held-out force/face gap shrinks 1.3-2x (uncertain; the val run will show). It also enables the group-averaged inference in L2.
proposals.risk: Capacity split: the non-equivariant 0.6M-parameter net must serve 48 orientations, so identity-view in-distribution error may rise 5-20% at equal steps (it may need more steps or F from 32 to 40). Errors in the transform tables are caught by the exactness test below. Adversarial directions are computed only for the identity view (recompute them for the drawn view on entry if needed).
proposals.cost: About 300 lines: the 48 transform tables (27-slot permutations, per-axis face permutations, the 125-entry signed moment permutation, R_h, kernel flips, owner/neighbour swap) plus 1-2 h of unit testing. Per-step overhead under 2%. No extra memory. A/B run: 2 x 20k steps, about 2 x 1.3 h.
proposals.test: (1) Exactness: use the existing rotated packets (*_rotswapxy, *_rotinvert) and their base geometries. The theta_h view on the base must match the identity view on the rotated packet to within fp32 rounding (energy relative difference <= 1e-5, the t_fast.py tolerance). (2) Scope gap: evaluate the current step-2 checkpoint on the banks of the 20 val geometries under 8 random views (zs_eval-style); expect large degradation. (3) A/B from the step-2 best checkpoint: 20k steps, max LR 3e-4, the s2_full pool schedule; arm A draws a random h each step, arm B uses the identity view. Measure per class (force/support/face/macro/grf and sensitivity): val means and max under the identity view and under 8 random views; worst-direction mu on 4 val geometries (Geo.adversarial); the evalnet gate (consistent + stress) on 2 test geometries, x and y. Pass: A's identity-view force/face val means <= 1.1x B's; A's random-view errors <= 1.2x its own identity-view errors (B is expected to be far worse); A's probe-vs-val gap smaller than B's.

proposals.title: Averaging several learned extensions (energy convexity guarantees no increase), with label-free Ritz weights and a disagreement indicator
proposals.component: inference (EnsembleOp over FastNet members: field / field_T / s_hat), usable in evalnet, diag_lat and zs_eval; also an adversarial-candidate generator
proposals.mechanism:
Setup. E_1..E_k are learned extensions of one geometry, each with the exact rigid split and exact port values. E_w = sum_i w_i E_i with sum w_i = 1 keeps the ports and the rigid part exact and stays linear in q. By Galerkin orthogonality, excess(Eq) = ||Eq - E*q||_K^2.
Guarantee. Energy convexity gives excess(E_avg q) = mean_i excess(E_i q) - mean_i ||E_i q - E_avg q||_K^2, so S <= S_hat(E_avg) <= mean_i S_hat(E_i) in Loewner order. The result is still symmetric PSD with the rigid kernel.
Ritz weights (label-free). G_ij = sum over q in Q of (E_i q)^T K (E_j q) / n(q), where Q contains macro, GRF and network-soft directions q = PCG(S_hat, f), and n(q) is any positive normalizer (for example the mean member energy). Since sum_q e_hat/n = w^T G w = constant + excess, the best weights are w* = G^{-1} 1 / (1^T G^{-1} 1). This is a k x k system, not a PDE solve; K enters only as in the readout.
Members. Now: independently trained r2 nets (mgno_r2_c v0, mgno2_r2_c, mgno2_r2_d2, and mgno2_r2_e when it finishes). After L1: O_h views of one augmented net (frame averaging, Puny et al., ICLR 2022, arXiv:2110.03336).
Indicator. d(q) = mean_i ||E_i q - E_avg q||_K^2 / e_avg(q) is a label-free lower bound on the members' mean excess. The top eigenvectors of D = sum_i (E_i - E_avg)^T K (E_i - E_avg), found by block power iteration in the S_hat metric, are label-free adversarial candidates.
Reaction and precedent. S_hat_w q = sum_i w_i E_i^T K (E_w q), built from the explicit adjoints already in fastnet. Deep ensembles (Lakshminarayanan et al., NeurIPS 2017) are the ML precedent; the guarantee here is specific to the energy readout.
proposals.addresses: The r2 y gate miss: test-cell sensitivity 3.10%, with the failing load interface-dominated (4.8% vs 1.0%). An S_hat closer to S in Loewner order directly reduces the interface error. Also the worst-direction mu of 1.31-1.48, and the absence of any label-free reliability signal for held-out geometries (step 2, design loops).
proposals.expected_gain: For two equal members whose field errors have correlation rho, the energy excess falls by a factor (1+rho)/2 and the first-order sensitivity error by sqrt((1+rho)/2). With rho = 0.5: -25% energy and -13% sensitivity, which would take r2 y from 3.10% to about 2.7% (a pass). Independent cold starts (v0 vs MGNO2) should be less correlated than d2/e, which share a warm start. Worst-direction mu falls by at least the members' disagreement in that direction.
proposals.risk: Correlated members give little gain. Unequal members need Ritz weights, which can overfit Q; keep k <= 4 and shrink the weights toward equal. Inference and adjoint cost scale by k, though each member is still 4-10 ms per direction. Training k step-2 nets costs k times as much; use the L1 views instead.
proposals.cost: About 60 lines. Zero training for the checkpoint-ensemble variant. About 1-2 h of evaluation on r2 (gate x/y, banks, adversarial search).
proposals.test: (1) Unit check: for every val direction, excess(E_avg q) <= mean_i excess(E_i q), and the decomposition identity holds to 1e-6 relative (fp64 energies). (2) r2: bank errors per class (force/support/face/macro/grf and sensitivity) for each member and for the equal-weight and Ritz-weight averages of {mgno_r2_c, mgno2_r2_c, mgno2_r2_d2} (plus e); worst-direction mu via Geo.adversarial with the averaged s_hat; the evalnet gate (consistent + stress) and the diag_lat decomposition. Pass: r2 y test-cell sensitivity <= 3.0% with every other gate item passing, and mu at least 10% lower than the best member's. (3) Indicator: on step-2 val geometries (4 L1 views), the Spearman correlation between d and the true force-class excess >= 0.6.

proposals.title: Gated discrete-extension head (AgFEM-style) for fictitious-fringe nodes
proposals.component: q-path output head (after the last fringe layer; latent variant before W_out) + a per-geometry geometric operator C in MGCache
proposals.mechanism:
C is a fixed geometric operator built per geometry from the grid, the weak flags and the element volume fractions. It uses no K, like the existing fixed trilinear transfers.
Construction. For each weak interior node w, the root r(w) is the best-supported active element within 2 elements: highest volume fraction first, then nearest; only non-weak nodes are used for fitting. This is the AgFEM root/aggregate (Badia, Verdugo & Martin, CMAME 2018). C_w holds the weights that evaluate the root's polynomial at x_w. Two variants:
- Q2 Lagrange: face-adjacent extrapolation factor <= 8 along one axis.
- Least-squares affine/Q1 on the root's non-weak nodes: factor <= 2, and it reproduces rigid motions and uniform strain exactly.
Head. u <- u + diag(g) M_w (C u - u), with g_w = sigmoid(head(gn_w, ge_r, d_w, vf_r)). g_w is one scalar per node, so it is isotropic and compatible with O_h. Its bias is initialised so that g is about 0.9 where every surrounding element has a volume fraction below 1e-3. Latent variant: the same relaxation on X before W_out, so the fringe layers learn the remainder. The map stays linear in q; ports stay exact (weak port nodes keep q, and the gate learns to open near them).
Mechanics. In an element held mainly by gamma-weighted jumps of normal derivatives, the energy minimiser in the fringe is the polynomial continuation of the well-supported neighbour. GP methods that penalise the distance to the aggregation-based extension converge to AgFEM (Badia, Neiva & Verdugo, CMAME 388 (2022) 114232, arXiv:2106.13728). The kernel of the GP operator is a discrete-extension finite element space (Burman, Hansbo & Larson, arXiv:2205.01340); DESIGN_mechanics.md part 4 describes the same picture. With the head, the network only has to learn the physical-region field, and the fringe follows a construction recomputed exactly for every new geometry. Precedent for a fixed extension plus a learned correction that keeps the boundary values: Haubner et al., CMAME 424 (2024), arXiv:2206.02217.
proposals.addresses: The fringe share of the step-1 error: 36% of force-direction error energy in the GP term and 45% of body error in fringe elements (r1 v0 block diagnosis). The stress-test inflation from fringe ports (FULL sensitivity 8.2-8.5%, r2 5.3-6.7%). The zero-shot energy blow-ups attributed to fringe/weak regions, whose distribution (18-22% of nodes) changes with geometry.
