proposals.expected_gain: If the oracle excess (test step 1) is <= 0.3%: about half of the fringe-attributed error energy should go, taking force/support bank error from about 2.0% to 1.3-1.6%, sensitivity error down 10-20%, and a lower worst mu wherever the worst mode sits in the fringe. On unseen geometries, the fringe's spurious energy is then bounded by the strong-node error times the extension constant (2-8), so fringe blow-ups should disappear. Any remaining zero-shot error is then attributable to the strong regions, which is a useful split in itself.
proposals.risk: gamma = 1e-4 is small, so the exact fringe field departs from pure continuation where the tiny cut body competes; the oracle may show 1-3%. Q2 extrapolation amplifies strong-node errors up to 8x. Roots are scarce in thin walls at volume fraction 0.1 (wall about 1.4 elements thick); fall back to a least-squares affine fit over a 2-element neighbourhood. Weak ports with independent data (the uniform-load stress test) conflict with slaving, so the gate must learn to open there.
proposals.cost: About 150 lines. C has 8-27 entries per weak node (roughly 5-100k rows), builds in under 1 s per geometry, and adds one sparse matvec to the forward and adjoint. Oracle test about 30 min GPU. r2 training A/B: 10k steps, about 1 h, plus the gate.
proposals.test: (0) Confirm the target: run diag_error.py on two zero-shot failures (r2 MGNO2 -> dev_0000 heavy cut; FULL 0020 -> dev_0002) and on 3 val geometries with the step-2 checkpoint, and report the share of the excess in the GP term and in fringe-element body terms. (1) Oracle, no training: take exact fields u* (teacher extend) for the val force/face/support/macro directions on r2 and on 4 step-2 geometries (2 heavy cuts, 1 medium, 1 FULL). Replace the weak-interior values by C u* (Q2 and least-squares affine; root thresholds vf >= 0.3 and 0.5) and compute excess = delta^T K delta at unit energy. Go/no-go on the mean: <= 0.3% hard slaving; <= 2% gated head; > 2% drop the proposal. (2) Train: MGNO2 + gated head, warm start mgno2_r2_d2, 10k steps, max LR 3e-4, d2 mix, against control arm e. Report bank val per class, the diag_error shares, worst mu, and the gate x/y + stress. Pass: force/face bank errors >= 15% below e, GP share halved (from about 36%), gate no worse. (3) Step 2: include the head in the next pool run and compare the val gap.

proposals.title: Lattice-context q class with DAgger-style on-policy aggregation
proposals.component: sampling / data (prep_geo + lattice3), trainer mix
proposals.mechanism:
New q class 'lattice'.
Configurations. For each training geometry g, build small lattices from g and its family's FULL parent, using configurations disjoint from the gate: neighbour glued at +x, +y or +/-z (the gate uses -x and -y), 3-cell chains, far faces clamped or on random springs (as in prep_support). Loads are random smooth tractions (plane waves or patches) on the free box faces, plus 10% on the cut surface.
Labels. Solve exactly with the lattice3 reference, take each cell's port displacement q_g, remove its rigid part, normalise to unit exact energy, and label exact sensitivities with the interior factor as in prep_geo.
On-policy variant (DAgger: Ross, Gordon & Bagnell, AISTATS 2011; used for composable energy surrogates by Beatson et al., NeurIPS 2020, arXiv:2005.06549). Every N steps, re-solve a subset of these lattices with the current network (PCG with S_hat, as in lattice3.evaluate) and add the network's q_g with exact labels. These are exactly the directions in which S_hat misleads the interface.
Mix: 15-20%, taken from the force share.
proposals.addresses: The last step-1 failure: r2 y nbr_facex0_z (the test cell holds 0.13% of the energy and is dragged almost rigidly) is interface-dominated, 4.8% vs 1.0% extension. The gap between banks and lattice (force bank 1.8-2.4% vs lattice sensitivity 2-3%). The largest past gains came from hand-made proxies for lattice context (support: r1 y 5.1% -> 1.22%; face: r2 y 4.42% -> 3.10%).
proposals.expected_gain: It targets the covariate shift directly instead of through proxies. Expected: the worst lattice sensitivity item falls to about bank level (~2%), the interface-only error of that load in diag_lat roughly halves, and the other classes' bank errors change little.
proposals.risk: Leakage for single-geometry step-1 nets if gate configurations are reused: the map is linear in q, so any load on a gate configuration spans the gate's q subspace. Keep configurations disjoint and document it. Lattice solves need the neighbour's exact data. Over-weighting near-rigid directions could cost face/force accuracy.
proposals.cost: About 150 lines on top of lattice3 and prep_geo. Data: about 20-60 s per geometry (a few lattices x 16-32 loads, dense port operators cached), so 1-2.5 h for 148 geometries. The on-policy refresh costs about one lattice solve per pool swap (seconds).
proposals.test: Step 1 (r2): warm start mgno2_r2_d2, 10k steps, max LR 3e-4, the d2 mix plus 15% lattice class (configurations disjoint from the gate), against arm e. Run the evalnet gate x/y (consistent + stress) and the diag_lat decomposition. Pass: y test-cell sensitivity <= 3% with nbr_facex0_z <= 2.5%; that load's interface-only error halved; other classes' bank errors within +10%. Step 2: add the class for the training geometries and run the gate on 2 test geometries.

proposals.title: Label-free test-time adaptation per geometry (energy loss only, with an exact label-free progress monitor)
proposals.component: inference / per-geometry trainer (fallback mode, clearly labelled)
proposals.mechanism:
Update. For a new geometry g, adapt theta for n Adam steps on L = mean_q log e_hat(q; theta, g), optionally plus the sensitivity term when exact dM is available. Adapt all weights, or only the geometry-path heads plus LoRA on W/Wf.
Why no labels are needed. e(q) = q^T S q does not depend on theta, so grad_theta log(e_hat/e) = grad_theta log e_hat. No labels and no solves are needed; exact K appears only in the loss, which is allowed.
Directions q, all label-free:
- macro and GRF (need only port coordinates);
- network-soft q = S_hat^+ f from 20-40 PCG iterations with the network's own S_hat and random smooth box/face forces (the label-free analogue of the force, support and face classes);
- the L2 disagreement eigenvectors.
Monitor. On a fixed probe set, the change in e_hat(q) equals the change in excess(q) exactly (e is fixed), so the achieved error reduction is measured without the teacher.
Precedents: PINO instance-wise fine-tuning with only the PDE loss (Li et al., ACM/IMS J. Data Sci. 2024, arXiv:2111.03794); test-time training (Sun et al., ICML 2020).
proposals.addresses: The held-out-geometry gap in step 2 (zero-shot 107-2236% for single-geometry nets; step-2 val pending), and design loops in which tau changes the geometry slightly (warm start from the previous design).
proposals.expected_gain: Per-geometry error should approach the training-geometry (probe) level. From scratch, step-1 nets went from 1.81 to 0.12 force error between steps 2k and 10k; from a step-2 warm start, 200-1000 steps should close most of the held-out gap. It also gives a label-free certificate that the error went down (not of the absolute error).
proposals.risk: Network-soft directions are biased (S_hat >= S) and may under-sample the true soft directions. The adaptation can overfit the probe distribution. LR must stay <= 3e-4: re-warming to 1e-3 wrecked a converged net (2.4% -> 10%). 15-120 s per geometry is too slow for 100 cells in every design iteration unless amortised (adapt once per family or tau band and warm start across iterations). Results differ per geometry, so this must be a labelled mode.
proposals.cost: About 100 lines. Per geometry: 100-500 steps x 0.15-0.23 s, plus PCG direction generation (about 0.1-0.3 s per 16 directions). Memory as in training.
proposals.test: Step-2 checkpoint; 6 val geometries stratified (2 heavy cuts, 2 medium, 2 FULL). Run 0/100/300/1000 adaptation steps at LR 1e-4 and 3e-4. Measure exact val banks per class plus sensitivity, worst mu (Geo.adversarial), and the gate on 2 test geometries. Pass: within 300 steps, force/face errors reach <= 1.5x the probe (training-geometry, unseen q) errors, no class gets worse by more than 10%, and the label-free change in e_hat tracks the exact error decrease to within fp32 noise.

proposals.title: Tail-aware objective: group DRO over geometries plus CVaR over directions
proposals.component: loss + sampling (train2.py pool admission and batch loss)
proposals.mechanism:
Geometry level (group DRO: Sagawa et al., ICLR 2020; hardness-weighted sampling: Fidon et al., arXiv:2001.02658). Keep an exponential moving average L_g of each training geometry's loss while it is in the pool. Admit the next pool member with probability p_g = (1 - rho)/N + rho * softmax(L_g/T), with rho = 0.5 and a cap of 3/N; unseen geometries go first.
Direction level. loss = (1 - lambda) * mean_b log e_b + lambda * CVaR_alpha, where CVaR_alpha is the mean of the top alpha fraction of log e_b; alpha = 0.25, lambda = 0.3. Apply it to the energy and sensitivity terms separately.
Keep weight decay and early stopping: Sagawa et al. find regularisation is needed for worst-group generalisation.
proposals.addresses: The gate is a maximum (every cell, every load <= 3%) while training minimises a mean. Worst-direction mu is 1.31-1.48 while bank means are about 2%. The step-2 first-entry worst ratios (106, 280, 46) show a heavy tail at the geometry level. train2's validation score is already the maximum over classes.
proposals.expected_gain: 10-30% lower p90 and maximum per-geometry val error, at a cost of at most 5-10% in the mean; smaller worst mu.
proposals.risk: It can chase noisy or degenerate geometries (the 5 with NaN support directions, slivers); cap the weights and exclude flagged geometries. CVaR amplifies the fp32 gradient noise (already 0.3-0.6%). It interacts with the pool schedule (fewer distinct geometries per hour).
proposals.cost: About 40 lines in train2.py. No memory cost. A/B: 2 x 20k steps.
proposals.test: From the step-2 checkpoint, 20k steps each with identical seeds: arm A = DRO + CVaR, arm B = current. On the 20 val geometries, measure per-geometry force/support/face/sensitivity mean, p90 and maximum; worst mu on 4 val geometries; and the first-entry worst ratios during training. Pass: maximum and p90 down >= 15%, mean within +10%.

proposals.title: Multiscale, topology-aware geometry encoder with gain control (only if the step-2 val strata call for it)
proposals.component: geometry path (encoder, slot/fslot/restriction/gate heads) + a small regulariser on the q-path residual stream
proposals.mechanism:
(a) Diagnostics first.
- Internal gain: rho_g = max_l ||X_l|| / ||X_out||, from an instrumented FastNet.ext, on training vs val geometries.
- Stratify the step-2 val errors by retained volume, volume fraction, weak fraction, the number of strong-node connected components (the K-sparsity graph restricted to non-weak nodes; islands attached only through weak nodes or GP faces), and minimum neck thickness.
(b) If the errors concentrate on geometries with islands or slivers, or rho_val >> rho_train:
- Geometry U-Net: pool gn to 33^3/17^3/9^3 with the existing c.trans weights, apply 2 nonlinear rounds per level, then unpool and concatenate into the slot/fslot/restriction/gate heads. The slot weights then see cell-scale context instead of about 2 elements.
- Topological node features: the component's volume fraction, touches-box and touches-cut flags, and graph distance to the nearest box port.
- Replace the absolute sin/cos coordinates with relative features (signed distance to the cut plane from the NETDATA normal/offset, distance to the box faces), or keep them only with the L1 transforms.
- Bound the slot heads, a = c * tanh(MLP/c).
- Add a kinetic penalty lambda * sum_l ||dX_l||^2 / ||X_0||^2 (Finlay et al., ICML 2020) against amplification-by-cancellation in the 24-layer linear residual stack (stable-architecture view: Haber & Ruthotto, Inverse Problems 2018; Eliasof, Haber & Treister, NeurIPS 2021).
Literature:
- RIGNO (arXiv:2501.19205): relative edge features, multiscale regional mesh.
- GAOT (arXiv:2505.18781) and MeshGraphNets.
- TNO (arXiv:2609.05860): topology changes alter the operator's invariant and decaying subspaces, and implicit handling degrades in 37 of 45 cases, so explicit topological priors are needed.
- arXiv:2606.08287: invariant encodings for unseen geometries.
proposals.addresses: Heavy-cut zero-shot failures (dev_0000 407% mean / 2151% maximum; r1 -> other heavy cuts 1e3x), where slivers and islands 'follow their anchor' non-locally (DESIGN_mechanics.md). FULL 0020 -> dev_0002 fails even in smooth classes (macro 1745%): a global mis-calibration that a 2-round local encoder cannot see. The first-entry worst ratios of 106-280.
proposals.expected_gain: Conditional. If the val errors are stratified by topology: 1.5-3x lower error on the island/sliver stratum. Otherwise small. The gain control mainly removes rare catastrophic entries (the tail of worst ratios).
proposals.risk: More geometry-path capacity can increase memorisation with only 148 geometries. The tanh caps may cost accuracy. The topology features are discontinuous in tau (a neck pinching off changes the components). The gate's sensitivities use -u^T dK u and do not differentiate through the geometry path, so this is acceptable for the gate, but it must be flagged for design use.
proposals.cost: Diagnostic about 1 h. Implementation about 150 lines. The geometry path costs 10-20% more per training step (it is recomputed every step); inference is unchanged after encoding (about +20 ms).
proposals.test: (1) On the step-2 checkpoint at 10k and 60k steps: the stratified val tables and rho_g. (2) If triggered, A/B from the step-2 checkpoint for 20k steps: val per-class errors per stratum, zero-shot on 4 more test-family geometries, worst mu. Pass: stratum error down >= 30% with the in-distribution (probe) error within +10%.

proposals.title: Residual certificate head: a rigorous solve-free lower bound on the error, learned sharpening, per-geometry μmax screen and a lattice compliance-error bound
proposals.component: readout by-product (r_I = (K u_hat)_I) + new small linear certificate head on the shared geometry trunk; inference (fastnet, zs_eval, evalnet)
proposals.mechanism:
Identity: u_hat has exact ports and Eq is K-harmonic, so K_II e_I = r_I and Δ(q) = q^T(S_hat - S)q = r_I^T K_II^-1 r_I (= e_hat - 1 at unit energy; diag_error's galerkin_check verifies it).

Certificate: for any w, Δ_lb(w) = (w^T r_I)^2 / (w^T K_II w) <= Δ, with equality iff w is parallel to e.
- It is rigorous for any w, even a nonlinear or inaccurate one, and uses fp64 dot products on the field actually evaluated.

Zero-parameter version: w = D_II^-1 r_I, using the 3x3 diagonal blocks already in NETDATA diag3.
- In D-scaled eigencoordinates, Δ_J/Δ = (Σc^2λ^2)^2 / (Σc^2λ^3 · Σc^2λ) (a Kantorovich-type ratio).
- It is sharp for band-limited, localized errors such as spurious fringe or ghost-penalty energy. It is loose for smooth soft-mode errors.

Learned version: w = D^-1 r + N_θ(g)(D^-1 r).
- N_θ is a linear MGNO-type map (F = 16; 2 element + 2 GP + 2 fringe layers + a 2-level U-Net) with new heads on the same geometry trunk.
- The branch is zero-initialised, so training starts exactly from the Jacobi certificate.
- Loss: 1 - Δ_lb/Δ, using the free label Δ = e_hat - 1 of every bank sample. u_hat is detached, so the main operator does not change.

Uses:
(a) Per query: ε_lb = Δ_lb / q^T S_hat q gives μ(q) >= 1/(1 - ε_lb).
(b) Per geometry: block Lanczos on the pencil (H, S_hat) with H = E_hat^T K J_I D^-1 J_I^T K E_hat, which needs only S_hat and K applies. Certifying the directions it finds with Δ_lb gives a rigorous lower bound on μmax with no factorization.
(c) Lattice: Σ_c Δ_lb,c(q_hat_c) <= U^T D U <= C - C_hat, a rigorous lower bound on the compliance error at the solution. It costs 1 head pass and 1 K apply per cell.

No cheap rigorous upper bound exists, because λmin(K_II) is tiny (weak nodes, γ = 1e-4). A 'probably good' estimate uses a conformal multiplier c_α fitted on validation geometries and is labelled as statistical.

Deployment policy: a flagged cell is replaced as a whole by the labelled fallback arm and is never locally corrected (see the Galerkin argument in the diagnosis). That routing lies outside the main line.
proposals.addresses:
Catastrophic cells on unseen geometries go unnoticed:
- zero-shot force errors 107-2236%, up to 2.8e3x;
- step-2 entry worst ratios 106/280/46/19.
Also: no μmax is available at deploy time (it currently needs an fp32 Neumann factor), and there is no error estimate at lattice level.
proposals.expected_gain:
- The Jacobi certificate should flag the catastrophic zero-shot and entry cases at zero training cost. For localized fringe spurious energy I expect Δ_J/Δ of order 0.1-1.
- The learned head targets a median Δ_lb/Δ >= 0.5 on force/support/face, i.e. error estimates sharp to within a factor of 2.
- A lower bound on μmax at deploy time in about 0.5-1.5 s per cell.
- A certified lower bound on the lattice compliance error.
- Main-line numbers do not change.
proposals.risk:
- The Jacobi bound will be loose for smooth errors; that is why the learned head exists.
- The learned head may be less sharp on out-of-family geometries. That affects sharpness only, never rigor.
- There is no rigorous upper bound.
- The proxy pencil may miss the true worst direction; the bound stays valid but is looser.
proposals.cost:
- Stage 0: about 1 h of scripting plus GPU time (an extension of zs_eval.py).
- Head: about 0.05-0.1M parameters, trained as a separate 5k-step stage on the frozen step-2 model: about 20-40 min and under 2 GB extra memory.
- Inference: 1 extra head pass + 1 K apply per certified query (about 2-5 ms). The geometry screen costs about 100-160 S_hat-equivalents per cell.

proposals.title: Lattice gate that matches deployment: all cells learned, with per-cell error accounting
proposals.component: inference/evaluation (evalnet.py, lattice3.py, diag_lat.py); consequence for loss targets
proposals.mechanism:
Galerkin identity: C - C_hat = U^T D U + U^T D A^-1 D U, where D = Σ_c J_c^T (S_hat_c - S_c) J_c >= 0.
- Hence ε_C lies in [Σ_c w_c ε_c, μmax · Σ_c w_c ε_c], where ε_c = μ_c(q_hat_c) - 1 >= 0 and w_c is the cell's energy share.
- The terms have one sign and add over learned cells.

Today only the test cell is learned, so ε_C ≈ w_test · ε_test with w_test = 0.13-0.41 on test loads and 0.0013-0.011 on neighbour loads.
- The per-cell excess in these lattice directions is therefore about 1.7-8x the reported compliance error.

Change: add an 'all-learned' configuration. lattice3.evaluate already takes a list of operators, so set ops = [FastOp(test net), FastOp(neighbour net)].
- Test cell: r2 MGNO2-d2 or r1 v0. Neighbour: the FULL0020 v0 network, their parent. For step 2, one network serves both cells.
- Log per-cell ε_c(q_hat_c) exactly (C.extend at q_hat_c) together with w_c, to check the accounting.
- Extend diag_lat to decompose both cells.

Consequence: in a lattice of learned cells, the per-cell excess in loaded directions must be about 1.5% or less, and μmax must come down, to keep margin. Current bank errors are 1.8-2.4% (force).
proposals.addresses:
- The current gate may overstate downstream accuracy, because errors from learned cells add and are not diluted by an exact neighbour.
- How to read the extension/interface cancellation.
- What the step-2 accuracy target should be.
proposals.expected_gain:
A decision-grade number now, at no training cost.

My prediction: compliance error in all-learned 2-cell lattices rises from 1.3-2.1% to about 2-3.5%, and neighbour-cell sensitivity error rises from 0.05-1.06% to about the 1.5-2% level of the FULL harness.

If the gate fails, the step-2 target and the class weights (adversarial/face) are reset before more compute is spent.
proposals.risk:
- Low; this is evaluation only.
- A 2-cell lattice still under-represents large lattices with more learned neighbours. A 3-cell chain needs a small extension of lattice3.build().
proposals.cost: About 1-2 GPU-hours. Dense T for FULL/r1/r2 is already cached (T64.npy). No training.
proposals.test:
Run evalnet with FastOp for both cells: consistent loads, configurations x and y, pairs (r2-d2, FULL v0) and (r1 v0, FULL v0), sensitivities of both cells.
- Pass: gate on compliance and on both cells' 8-corner sensitivities (<= 3%).
- Accounting check: the measured ε_C lies in [Σ w_c ε_c, μmax · Σ w_c ε_c] on all loads.

Then repeat with the step-2 checkpoint on the 4 validation families, with each family's FULL parent also learned.

proposals.title: Trainer: unbiased probe, cheap and frequent geometry rotation, leaner activation memory
proposals.component: trainer (train2.py, sparse_layers.HyperFn), sampling (adversarial refresh)
proposals.mechanism:
(a) Probe fix, immediate. Evaluate two probe sets:
- P_early = order[:12] (visited in steps 0-3.9k);
- P_recent = the 12 most recently admitted geometries.
Forgetting = err(P_early) - err(P_recent). Generalization gap = err(val) - err(P_recent).

(b) Memory:
- In HyperFn, recompute Z = G X and Zp = Z W in backward instead of saving them (+1 sparse matmul and +1 batched matmul per layer).
- Checkpoint the fine-layer stack every 4 layers, keeping X only at block boundaries.
- Estimate for a 430k-DOF geometry at batch 16: about 13-14 GB of activations drops to about 3-5 GB.

(c) Swaps:
- An async host thread loads the next slot, so the 2-5 s load leaves the critical path.
- Only banks['train'] go to the GPU.
- The adversarial block is computed with the fp32 Neumann factor only on a geometry's first visit and kept with the slot on the host.
- Later visits reuse it after one Rayleigh-Ritz refresh on S_hat. No factor is needed, and no exact renormalisation either, because the gradient of log e_hat is scale-invariant. Alternatively they can use D1's solve-free pencil.

(d) Schedule: swap every 50 steps instead of 300, pool 4-5 under the DOF cap. Visits per geometry go from about 1.4 to about 8 at the same total exposure.

Optional: sample geometries in proportion to their certified μ_lb,max from D1.
proposals.addresses:
- The 28.4 GB peak and the pool limit of 3.
- 13% swap + adversarial overhead.
- About 1.4 visits per geometry with about 44k-step gaps (non-iid sampling, risk of forgetting).
- A biased probe of the generalization gap.
proposals.expected_gain:
- Peak memory from about 28 GB to about 17-20 GB (estimate).
- Swap overhead from 13% to 3% or less.
- No factorization in the steady state.
- Much better interleaving of geometries. The validation gain is uncertain; it is likely only if the measured forgetting gap is large, and (a) measures it.
proposals.risk:
- Recompute and checkpointing add about 10-25% step time.
- Stale adversarial blocks may be less effective.
- Gradients must be checked (equal to the 0.3-0.6% run-to-run noise, as in the earlier sparse-layer check).
proposals.cost: 0.5-1 day of engineering. Step time about 0.23 s -> 0.26-0.28 s. No new data.
proposals.test:
(a) At the next evaluation, report P_early vs P_recent vs val per class. If err(P_early) - err(P_recent) > 0.5 point, forgetting matters.

(b) A/B from the same step-2 checkpoint, 10k steps each: A = current schedule, B = new trainer.
- Pass: B <= A on every class mean over the 20 validation geometries and on P_early.
- Peak memory <= 20 GB.
- Wall-clock within +10%.
- Gradient check within run-to-run noise.

proposals.title: Continuous, geometry-local node features with soft fringe gating, plus the consistent surrogate gradient
proposals.component: geometry path (node features in prep_data.netdata / MGCache.nfeat, MGNO2 fringe masks)
proposals.mechanism:
- Replace the hard weak flag with a soft score s_i = σ((log10(||D_i|| / d_ref(t_i)) + 2) / 0.15). Here d_ref(t) is the analytic ||D|| of a fully solid node of Q2 type t (vertex/edge/face/centre, from grid parity). It is a single constant for n = 32, E, ν, the same for all 194 definitions (V01).
- Replace log(||D|| / median) with log(||D_i|| / d_ref(t_i)). This feature is local and means the same thing in every geometry.
- Run the fringe layers on a fixed superset mask {max over nodes of s_i > 1e-3} per design band, and multiply their slot weights a, b by a smooth max of s over the hyperedge. Hyperedges then fade in continuously.
- As a result, E_hat(τ), S_hat(τ) and C_hat(τ) are continuously differentiable inside a topology.
- The consistent gradient dC_hat/dτ = s(u_hat) - 2Σ_c r_I,c^T (∂E_hat_I,c/∂τ) q_hat_c then comes from one reverse pass through moments_ad (already exact) + geometry path + q path, with r_I held fixed.
- Deliver both s(u_hat), the gate quantity, and dC_hat/dτ, the optimizer's consistent gradient. Choose between them by measurement.
proposals.addresses:
- C_hat jumps inside a fixed topology when nodes cross the 1% threshold (it is both a feature and a fringe mask).
- Per-geometry median normalisation shifts features between geometries, a candidate cause of the fringe-localised zero-shot blow-ups.
- There is no consistent gradient for MMA/OC line searches.
proposals.expected_gain:
- A continuous surrogate for the design loop.
- A consistent objective/gradient pair.
- Possibly lower cross-geometry error in fringe regions; the size is unknown and the A/B measures it.
proposals.risk:
- The accuracy shift is small but needs a warm fine-tune at LR 3e-4 (not 1e-3, given the d-arm lesson).
- dC_hat/dτ may be further from the exact dC/dτ than s(u_hat) if the network's relative error varies with τ.
- The superset mask adds a little fringe work.
proposals.cost:
- Features and mask: trivial compute, recomputed on the fly from diag3, no teacher rerun.
- Fine-tune: 5-10k steps (0.5-1 h).
- dC_hat/dτ per cell per design iteration: one reverse pass (0.1-0.3 s) + moments_ad backward (measured 1.1/2.9/4.9 s for r1/r2/FULL).
proposals.test:
(i) Continuity. On r2, FULL0020 and 2 step-2 validation geometries, perturb each of the 8 τ corners by ±h (h relative 1e-2 down to 1e-5) with the element set held fixed. Rebuild moments, K and features, and solve the lattice with the learned cell.
- Count weak-flag flips and jumps, defined as |C_hat(τ+h) - C_hat(τ-h)| > 10 · (2h |dC_hat/dτ| + 1e-7 C_hat).
- Pass: zero jumps after the change (the baseline is expected to show some), and the finite difference of C_hat matches the autograd dC_hat/dτ to 1e-3.

(ii) On the gate loads, report the relative error vs exact dC/dτ for both s(u_hat) and dC_hat/dτ.

(iii) Regression: validation bank errors per class within +0.1 point; lattice gate unchanged within 0.2 point.

proposals.title: Lean, batched lattice inference engine computing the same map
proposals.component: inference (fastnet), readout K apply
proposals.mechanism:
Tier 1:
- One CSR pattern per hyperedge set (element, GP, fringe-element, fringe-GP), with the p1/p2 permutations of sparse_layers.pattern, shared by all layers of that set.
- Per layer, store only the α and β values: 8 B per nonzero instead of 32 B for G, S, Gt and St. Form the four value arrays by gathers on the fly.

Tier 2:
- Keep only the trunk embeddings ge/gn/gf (about 40 MB per FULL cell) and recompute the slot-head MLPs inside each apply (about 35 GFLOP fp32, deterministic, about 1 ms).

Stiffness:
- Replace the fp64 upper CSR plus transposed copy (about 2.4 GB per FULL cell) with a matrix-free apply.
- Body part: from the 125 moments per element and the fixed Tm templates, reassociated per element chunk as in sens2.
- Ghost part: γ times a fixed ghost-face template per axis, since ∂K_ghost/∂τ = 0 according to the design docs.
- Accumulate in fp64 as now.

Cross-cell batching:
- Every cell uses the same 33^3/17^3/9^3 grids, so conv3d runs once for all cells with batch = cells x B.
- Hyperedge sparse matmuls become block-diagonal concatenations.

CUDA-graph capture of ext/ext_T per (cell group, B).
proposals.addresses:
- About 1.2 GB network record + 2.4 GB K per FULL-size cell (estimate), so a 100-cell lattice (about 360 GB) cannot be resident.
- Single-direction applies partly limited by launch overhead (r1 3.8 ms vs 1.4 ms/direction at 64; r2 9.5 vs 5.7 ms).
- A design iteration with 100 medium cells x about 50 BDD iterations x 9 loads at 57 ms takes about 5 min for the network alone.
proposals.expected_gain:
- Resident memory per FULL-size cell: about 0.35 GB (tier 1) or about 0.1 GB (tier 2), estimates. 100-cell lattices then fit on 32 GB.
- 2-3x lower single-direction latency and at least 2x throughput from cross-cell batching (estimates).
- The operator is the same up to fp32 rounding, so results do not silently change.
proposals.risk:
- Tier 2 adds about 10-30% compute per apply.
- The matrix-free K is slower than a CSR sparse matmul unless it is fused.
- The ghost-template assumption must be checked against GP_UPPER.
- Engineering complexity.
- Moving to n = 64 would need a fourth U-Net level with new conv weights.
proposals.cost: 2-4 days of engineering. No training.

proposals.title: Learned SPD Neumann action (BDD preconditioner) on the shared trunk
proposals.component: new q-path head (inference, lattice solver)
proposals.mechanism:
- M_c = Π_Γ B_θ^T B_θ Π_Γ, where Π_Γ is the exact rigid projector on the ports and B_θ is a linear MGNO-type map from port forces to a latent node field (its own W, heads on the shared geometry trunk).
- M_c is positive semidefinite by construction and its kernel contains the rigid modes. One application costs about one forward + one adjoint pass and needs no K.
- Train after the operator is frozen, with the label-free loss L = E_v ||v - M S_hat v||^2_S_hat / ||v||^2_S_hat. Take v from the bank classes, D1/adversarial directions and random vectors; only S_hat applies are needed.
- Optionally supervise on force samples: f = S q is computed in normalize() during data prep but not stored; store it in future prep runs.
- Lattice solver: balanced BDD with a rigid-mode coarse space and M_c as the local Neumann solve.
- For any SPD M, PCG/BDD converges to the same S_hat solution. Accuracy is unchanged; only the iteration count depends on the condition number of M S_hat.
proposals.addresses:
- lattice3 preconditions with an exact dense lattice Cholesky, which works only for 2 cells.
- Exact per-cell Neumann factors would defeat the purpose of the learned operator (an fp32 factor is about 6.6 GB for a FULL cell).
- Forward-only preconditioning needed 300-1600 iterations in route 1.
proposals.expected_gain:
- A lattice solve with no factorization, with iteration counts near exact BDD (target <= 1.5x, about 20-60 iterations), scaling to large lattices.
- This completes a fully learned downstream pipeline for step 3.
proposals.risk:
- Medium.
- Under the XP port convention, heavy cuts add many soft private cut-band unknowns (for example 6.9k band nodes vs 1.8k box nodes at retained volume 0.148), and M must capture them. This interacts with the open XP/XB decision (O2).
- Training costs about 3 S_hat applies per sample.
proposals.cost: About 0.3M parameters; 2-4 h of training on the step-2 pool. Per iteration about 0.6x an S_hat apply per cell.

reviews.reason: The structural facts check out. GP_FACES has neighbour = owner + e_axis, so the owner is the lower cell. models.py:330-333 keeps owner layers 1-2 plus the neighbour's middle layer, i.e. global layers 1-3 of 0-4. The Q2 jumps [d_n u] ~ (-1,4,-6,4,-1) and [d_n^2 u] ~ (-1,2,0,-2,1) do need layers 0 and 4. Four claims are overstated. (1) The (1,3) node pair is also GP-only and is already in the stencil. (2) Because element layers (layers 0-2 and 2-4) alternate with face layers, the stack can compose the 5-layer functional. The limit is per-layer expressiveness, not what the network can represent. (3) 'MGNO2 gain came from capacity, not GP structure' has no ablation behind it. (4) The 36% GP share was measured on r1 v0, which has no face layers; MGNO2's share is unknown. The J (x) I3 Kronecker form is unverified: DATA_INTERFACE calls 54 = 9x3x2 a guess, and the templates are not local. Cost is underestimated: there are ~1.7x more ghost faces than elements (21.9k vs 12.9k in FULL), and face layers are 12 of the 24, so +67% face work means roughly +30-45% step time and more pattern/activation memory at a 28.4/31.4 GB peak.

Label-free on-policy lattice training (a refinement of L4/P2c). By the envelope theorem, the gradient of the network lattice compliance C_hat is the energy gradient at fixed q_hat. Maximising C_hat (C - C_hat = ||u - u_hat||_a^2 >= 0) is therefore an on-policy energy loss that needs only K and the network's own lattice solve, with no exact lattice solution. Exact solves are needed only for sensitivity labels.

The sensitivity gate has a first-order error component that Galerkin pairing does not protect. With dK/dtau = cK + K_perp on cut elements, the total sensitivity error is 2c||u - u_hat||_a^2 - 2 u^T K_perp (u_hat - u). Only the energy-like part cancels between extension and interface. So lattice-context sensitivity labels (glue class) matter more than reweighting the bank sensitivity loss.

missing: Checkpoint retention: train2 overwrites last.pt at every EVAL (train2.py:307) and ckpt.pt every 2k steps, and best.pt is chosen only by max class-mean ENERGY. Many proposals assume 10k/20k checkpoints of the running job exist. Add an external watcher now that copies last.pt to step-tagged files after each EVAL; it does not touch the running process.

Interference with the running v1 job: there is one 31.4 GB GPU, and v1 peaks at ~28.4 GB. Any concurrent diagnostic that factorizes (diag_error's interior factor, adversarial search, oracle C.extend, Neumann Ritz values on 206 geometries) risks OOM-killing v1. A guard-script resume would also change the RNG stream (gen = default_rng([seed, step])), and v1 would stop being a clean control. Rule: only CPU/log diagnostics while v1 runs (G3 test 0, P6 components, G2 voxel check, SPLIT leakage); everything on the GPU afterwards.

step-2 validate() measures only mean energy per class. It has no sensitivity, p90, max, mu or per-family breakdown, while the gate binds on sensitivity. v1's best.pt may therefore not be the gate-best model. A post-hoc eval of the snapshots with sensitivity is needed, and v2's validate() must include these metrics.

Statistical power of model selection: val has only 4 families (20 geometries). Family-level variation likely dwarfs the 0.3-0.6% gradient noise, and choosing among ~10 arms on the same 4 families invites selection overfitting. Require the same direction of change on >= 3 of 4 families plus 2 seeds for any winner. Keep the 38 test geometries untouched; L1, L5 and D1 propose using test geometries during development.

Step-1 pass/fail hinges on a single gate item (r2 y nbr_facex0_z, 3.10% against 3.0%), and ±0.2-0.3 pt run-to-run noise on that item is plausible. Judge on the distribution over all 12 gate loads plus the stress test, with 2 seeds.

Wrong control arm: several proposals name 'arm e' as control, but e lacks the face class. Use one shared continuation control for all step-1 A/Bs (d2 + 10k steps, same mix, seed and LR 3e-4); it can serve ~5 arms. Likewise use one shared 10-20k continuation from v1 final for all step-2 arms.

Engineering tax of q-path changes: each one must be mirrored in three implementations (models dense path, sparse_layers custom backward, fastnet explicit adjoint) and re-verified with t_fast. At equal promise, prefer geometry-path-only changes (G1a, G3, stiffness-share scaling folded into b), which reuse the unchanged verified kernels.

No pre-registered decision rule at v1's 10k/20k EVAL. Suggested rules:
- If val force mean is below ~5% with per-geometry max/median below 3: prioritize step-1 accuracy items (obj-P4, obj-P2) and G4, and deprioritize G1/G2.
- If a catastrophic tail persists on held-out families: run G1a and the G5 monitor first.
- If a large held-out vs recently-visited gap remains after the forgetting correction: run G4 and consider geometry multiplication.
